jobs.description:
Consultant (Associate Track)

About LunchAssist

LunchAssist supports school nutrition leaders by simplifying compliance, strengthening programs, and providing high-quality training and tools. We work with 500+ school districts and operate at the intersection of school nutrition, compliance, and technology. We are a growing, California-certified, small, woman-owned business staffed by a badass team of school nutrition neRDs.

We provide consulting to school districts in California, advising across all areas of the School Nutrition Program (SNP) and the Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP). We also offer training to school districts nationwide through online courses, live webinars, bilingual training videos, resources, and a proprietary software called LunchAssist PRO, which meets USDA professional standards and training requirements.

Overview

This role is designed for individuals who are ready to become high-impact consultants in school nutrition. At LunchAssist, consulting goes beyond technical expertise. Members of our team learn how to translate knowledge into clear guidance, training, and problem-solving across diverse districts. We provide accurate guidance to nutrition directors that is actually useful. Our clients come to us because we cut through government jargon and help them apply program regulations in ways that make sense for their operations and mitigate the risk of compliance issues down the road.

Our virtual workplace is fast-paced, highly collaborative, and impact-oriented. Successful candidates will bring strong experience in school nutrition programs, along with the humility to understand that consulting requires a distinct professional skill set. New hires will learn how to translate their expertise into effective client advisory, training, and problem-solving across all areas of the SNP and CACFP.

Associate Track

All new consultants enter a structured development period similar to supervised practice in a new specialty. New hires join a collaborative consulting pod where they immediately contribute by executing key components of client work. New hires will spend 12-18 months on this “Associate Track”, eventually building the confidence and skills to lead client relationships.

The Associate Track is designed to build:

  • Client advisory and communication skills
  • Problem-solving across varied district environments
  • Technical depth and breadth of knowledge across all SNP and CACFP program areas
  • Confidence and good judgment required for independent client management

During the first 12-18 months, new consultants on the Associate Track will support clients by:

  • Drafting client communications and follow-ups
  • Preparing action items from meetings and compliance documentation
  • Supporting menu planning, nutrient analysis, and crediting of recipes
  • Supporting SNP/CACFP Administrative and Procurement Reviews
  • Assisting with special projects, resource management tools, and state reporting
  • Contributing to both strategy and execution
  • Providing coverage to more experienced consultants when they are on leave

At LunchAssist, we are committed to building a team of school nutrition consultants who combine a wide breadth of programmatic knowledge, deep subject-matter expertise, and high-trust client advisory skills. We believe that great consultants are developed through guided, hands-on practice and peer-to-peer mentorship, not just prior experience in school nutrition.

Over time, consultants assume increasing responsibility, including leading portions of client interactions and progressing toward full client management.

Consulting at LunchAssist is both strategic and hands-on.

All consultants:

  • Operate within pods and contribute to shared delivery
  • Engage in both execution and advisory work
  • Maintain a balance of client work and internal contributions

In addition to client work, consultants contribute to internal priorities such as:

  • Developing training materials and resources
  • Supporting webinars and conferences
  • Improving tools, systems, and content

This work is a core component of the role and supports scalability across the organization.

As consultants progress, responsibilities include:

  • Supporting and leading client meetings (primarily via Zoom)
  • Advising school nutrition directors on USDA and State requirements (CDE)
  • Preparing clients for Administrative and Procurement Reviews
  • Contributing to projects (e.g., CEP/P2, bids and procurement, farm-to-school)
  • Developing training materials, tools, and resources
  • Speaking at webinars and conferences
  • Supporting and mentoring new consultants

Requirements

Must Have:

  • Bachelor's Degree
  • Registered Dietitian and/or previous employment by a State Agency conducting SNP Administrative Reviews
  • 5+ years of experience in school nutrition (district, State, or USDA)
  • Strong menu planning and compliance experience
  • Strong communication skills (with an emphasis on digital communications such as Zoom & email)
  • Demonstrated problem-solving ability and attention to detail
  • Organized, adaptable, collaborative, resourceful, and humble

Preferred:

  • Native or fluent Spanish proficiency, with the ability to deliver training and consulting in Spanish

Who Thrives in This Role:

  • Growth-oriented individuals interested in consulting and who enjoy detailed, hands-on work
  • School nutrition professionals who value both strategy and execution
  • Strong communicators who build trust with clients and connect well with school nutrition leaders

Compensation

The salary range for this role is $75,000-$100,000. We typically start at the bottom of the range, and new hires have the opportunity for rapid salary growth based on performance and business needs.

Benefits

  • 15 vacation days, 14 holidays, 8 sick days
  • 401(k) with 4% match (immediate vesting)
  • Medical, dental, vision, short-term disability, and life insurance
  • $100/month home office stipend

Schedule & Work Environment

  • Full-time, exempt, remote (must provide home office set up, including computer)
  • Must be able to travel 10% of the time for conferences, in-person client meetings, or trainings
  • Availability required until 5:30 p.m. Pacific Time (prefer candidates located in the Western U.S.)

Apply

Please submit an application via Breezy HR. Due to high application volume, not all applicants will receive a response. Selected candidates will be contacted for interviews.
Salary: $75,000 – $100,000 / year

The Business Operations Manager helps teams work more effectively by managing essential operational activities, improving business processes, and strengthening the tools and information that support day-to-day work. This hands-on individual contributor takes ownership of assigned responsibilities, coordinates across teams, and turns operational challenges into practical, sustainable solutions.

Position Type: Full-Time, Remote
Working Hours: U.S. Eastern Time (EST)

About the Role

At Pavago, one of our clients is hiring a Sales Account Executive to drive new business, manage the full B2B sales cycle, and build strong client relationships.

This is a hands-on, full-cycle sales role for someone who can take an opportunity from initial outreach through signed agreement.

You’ll be responsible for:

  • Prospecting and generating new business
  • Running discovery calls and sales presentations
  • Managing opportunities through the pipeline
  • Negotiating and closing deals
  • Building long-term client relationships
  • Consistently achieving revenue targets

If you have a proven sales track record, communicate confidently with decision-makers, and enjoy owning revenue outcomes, this role is a strong fit.

What You’ll Own

Full-Cycle B2B Sales

Own the complete sales process from prospecting through close:

  • Prospecting
  • Outreach
  • Qualification
  • Discovery calls
  • Sales presentations
  • Follow-up
  • Negotiation
  • Closing

Identify new business opportunities and maintain consistent activity across every stage of the sales funnel.

Pipeline Generation & Management

  • Build and maintain a healthy pipeline of qualified opportunities.
  • Generate new business through proactive prospecting and follow-up.
  • Prioritize opportunities based on fit, intent, and revenue potential.
  • Maintain strong follow-up discipline to keep deals moving.
  • Track pipeline activity, next steps, and expected close dates.

Discovery & Consultative Selling

  • Conduct structured discovery calls with prospective clients.
  • Understand business needs, pain points, priorities, and buying motivations.
  • Ask thoughtful questions to identify the right solution.
  • Tailor sales conversations and presentations to each prospect.
  • Communicate business value clearly rather than relying on feature-based selling.

Sales Presentations & Closing

  • Deliver professional sales presentations and solution recommendations.
  • Build credibility with business owners and decision-makers.
  • Handle objections confidently and professionally.
  • Negotiate pricing and commercial terms within approved guidelines.
  • Drive qualified opportunities toward clear decisions and successful closes.

Client Relationship Management

  • Build strong relationships with prospects and clients.
  • Maintain professional communication throughout the sales process.
  • Understand client goals and recommend appropriate solutions.
  • Support smooth transitions after the sale.
  • Identify opportunities for repeat business, referrals, or account growth where applicable.

CRM & Sales Reporting

Maintain accurate CRM records covering:

  • Prospect interactions
  • Sales activities
  • Pipeline stages
  • Follow-ups
  • Deal values
  • Next steps
  • Expected close dates

Provide leadership with clear visibility into pipeline health, sales activity, and revenue opportunities.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

Work closely with internal teams to:

  • Ensure smooth client handoffs after closing.
  • Communicate customer expectations accurately.
  • Share prospect and market feedback.
  • Support broader sales and revenue goals.
  • Identify opportunities to improve the sales process.

Required Experience & Skills

Must-Have

  • 3+ years of experience in Sales, Account Management, Business Development, or a related revenue-generating role.
  • Proven ability to close deals and achieve revenue targets.
  • Experience managing the full sales cycle.
  • Strong pipeline management and follow-up discipline.
  • Experience using CRM systems.
  • Excellent written and verbal English communication.
  • Strong negotiation and objection-handling skills.
  • Ability to build relationships with business owners and decision-makers.
  • Self-motivated, competitive, and results-oriented.
  • Comfortable working independently in a remote environment.
  • Availability to work EST hours.

Nice-to-Have Experience

  • B2B sales experience.
  • Service-based sales experience.
  • Experience selling to business owners or senior decision-makers.
  • Remote sales experience.
  • Experience generating your own pipeline.
  • Consultative or solution-selling experience.
  • Strong forecasting and reporting skills.
  • Stable employment history with demonstrated career progression.

What Makes You a Strong Fit

You:

  • Enjoy both prospecting and closing.
  • Are confident leading sales conversations.
  • Know how to uncover a prospect’s actual business needs.
  • Build relationships without losing focus on revenue outcomes.
  • Follow up consistently and keep opportunities moving.
  • Are comfortable handling objections and negotiating.
  • Think in terms of pipeline, conversion, and revenue.
  • Take ownership of your targets rather than waiting for opportunities to come to you.
  • Thrive in fast-paced, performance-driven environments.

What a Typical Day Looks Like

A Sales Account Executive’s day may include:

  • Prospecting for new business opportunities.
  • Following up with active leads.
  • Running discovery calls.
  • Delivering sales presentations.
  • Speaking with business owners and decision-makers.
  • Handling objections and negotiating deals.
  • Moving opportunities through pipeline stages.
  • Updating CRM records and next steps.
  • Reviewing pipeline health and sales performance.
  • Coordinating internally on newly closed clients.

In short: you build pipeline, develop relationships, close deals, and directly drive revenue growth.

Key Metrics for Success

  • Monthly and quarterly revenue generated
  • Sales quota attainment
  • Qualified pipeline generated
  • Lead-to-opportunity conversion rate
  • Opportunity-to-close conversion rate
  • Number and value of deals closed
  • Pipeline health and deal velocity
  • CRM accuracy and reporting discipline
  • Client relationship quality and retention

Why This Role Stands Out

  • Fully remote opportunity.
  • Full ownership of the sales cycle.
  • Direct impact on company revenue.
  • Opportunity to work closely with leadership.
  • Performance-driven environment with strong earning potential.
  • High autonomy and ownership.
  • Career growth opportunities into:
    • Senior Account Executive
    • Enterprise Account Executive
    • Sales Manager
    • Business Development Manager
    • Sales Leadership

Interview Process

  • Initial Screening Call
  • Recruiter Interview
  • Final Client Interview
  • Background Verification
  • Offer & Onboarding

Spark Hire Intro Video

As part of the application process, you’ll be asked to complete a short Spark Hire intro video.

We’re particularly interested in hearing about:

  • Your B2B sales experience.
  • The products or services you’ve sold.
  • Your experience owning the full sales cycle.
  • How you generate and manage pipeline.
  • Your approach to discovery, objection handling, and closing.
  • Your track record against sales or revenue targets.
  • An example of a deal you successfully moved from initial conversation through close.

Keep your responses clear, concise, and conversational. We want to understand how you communicate with prospects, build relationships, and approach sales opportunities.

Completion of the Spark Hire intro video is required for your application to be considered.

Apply Now

If you:

  • Have 3+ years of sales experience.
  • Have a proven ability to close deals and hit targets.
  • Enjoy full-cycle B2B sales.
  • Are confident communicating with decision-makers.
  • Take ownership of pipeline and revenue.
  • Thrive in target-driven environments.

We’d love to hear from you.

Apply today and complete the required Spark Hire intro video to move forward in the hiring process.

jobs.title: Integration Associate, Clinic Acquisitions
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote - Athens

Remote role based in Athens, covering mostly US East Coast hours (afternoons and evenings in Athens). Independent contractor engagement at $3,500–$4,500 per month (USD), depending on experience. As a contractor, you’ll invoice us monthly and handle your own taxes and social security contributions.

ABOUT 3Y HEALTH

3Y Health is building the operating system for healthcare practices, an AI-native platform that helps clinicians start, run and grow their practice. We work as a managed services organization (MSO): along with the software, our operations team runs the back office for the clinics we partner with, including billing, insurance and compliance. We currently serve applied behavior analysis (ABA) therapy practices and are expanding into other specialties. We're backed by over $200mm from Founders Fund, General Catalyst, SoftBank and 8VC.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We enter new markets by acquiring a foundational clinic for each specialty and region we go into, and we partner with independent clinics across the country. Every clinic adds entities, filings, contracts, staff records and deadlines that need to stay in order.

In this role, you'll own a set of our entities from start to finish. When we acquire a clinic, you'll carry out its integration plan: collect and file the records, prepare the filings, get staff ready for day one and follow up with everyone until each item is closed. Each deal comes with a detailed plan and timeline from the deal lead. Acquired clinics keep running largely as they do today until we bring them onto our platform, usually within a few months. Once a clinic is integrated, you'll keep its entity in good standing, alongside the existing entities you own.

You don't need experience in US healthcare. Every deal comes with a detailed checklist, and we'll teach you the US specifics. You need to learn fast, care about details and follow through. You'll work closely with our Corporate Development, Legal, Billing and HR teams in the US, and with a teammate in the same role.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Acquisitions

  • Work through each deal's integration checklist from before signing through the first months after close, keep the tracker current, and flag anything at risk of slipping

  • Document how the clinic runs today, such as scheduling, intake, referrals and billing handoffs

  • Check that each acquired entity is in good standing, and that its legal name and tax ID match across IRS, state, bank and payer records

  • Support our team and advisors on payer change-of-ownership notices, Medicare enrollment updates and credentialing checks

  • Map every payer's electronic payment setup (EFT/ERA) and each clinic's bank accounts, so our billing team can keep cash flowing through close

  • Prepare staff for day one: verify the employee roster, gather employment records for legal review, run license and exclusion checks, collect onboarding paperwork securely, and help get payroll, benefits and staff FAQs ready

  • Inventory each clinic's vendors, software and logins, collect business associate agreements (BAAs) for legal review, and track which systems switch to ours at close, later or not at all

  • Follow through after close on staff communication, moving patients of departing providers to remaining clinicians, lease and facility license items, and the former owners' transition commitments

Entity management and corporate operations

  • Keep the entities you own in good standing, primarily by managing our vendors: prepare annual reports, state registrations, IRS updates and other filings, and track them to on-time filing with our legal team

  • Maintain entity records, including formation documents, officers, registered agents and ownership

  • Prepare and submit provider and facility enrollments with state Medicaid programs and other public payers, and track them to approval

  • Make sure incoming mail for your entities is logged, routed and acted on, especially anything with a deadline

  • Prepare contracts from templates, route them for signature, and keep our contract management system and renewal dates current

  • Note what worked and what didn't, so our checklists get better with each deal

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

  • 2–5 years in healthcare operations, practice management, credentialing or provider enrollment, or acquisition integration

  • A track record of managing many details and deadlines to completion

  • Comfort working with contracts, licenses and government forms. You read carefully and catch errors.

  • Strong spreadsheet skills, and quick to learn new systems

  • Excellent written and spoken English. Most of your work is with US teams, agencies and vendors, and most decisions happen in writing.

  • Comfort handling confidential information

  • High agency and low ego. You don't need to be chased, and you'll do the tedious work as carefully as the interesting work.

  • Based in Athens and able to work mostly US East Coast hours (afternoons and evenings in Athens)

NICE TO HAVE

  • Experience in US healthcare, insurance or another regulated industry

  • Experience working with US companies or customers

  • Experience with corporate filings, contract administration or compliance work

  • Daily use of AI tools such as Claude or ChatGPT to work faster

WHAT WE OFFER

  • A monthly fee of $3,500–$4,500 (USD), depending on experience

  • A long-term role at a venture-backed US company, working closely with leadership

  • Room to grow as we acquire more clinics and enter new specialties

ENGAGEMENT

This is a long-term independent contractor engagement with 3Y Health, not an employment contract. You'll need to be registered as a freelancer in Greece, or be willing to register before your start date. You'll be paid monthly in USD.

If you meet most of the requirements and the role interests you, we'd like to hear from you, even if you don't check every box.

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/3y-health-integration-associate-clinic-acquisitions

jobs.title: Win-back Specialist
jobs.description:
About Decentralized Masters

Decentralized Masters is an investment education and research company. We went from two co-founders to 160+ people and 4,500+ paying members in four years, bootstrapped and profitable. Our business is built on continuity: high-ticket and low-ticket programmes that are membership-based, with payment plans, renewals, upsells and a paid newsletter. We have never taken outside capital. Our growth is still heavily direct-response: paid media on Facebook, YouTube and Google feeds the webinars, calls and offers that fund everything we do.

Our vision is to become the gold standard in investment education and research.

The Role

The Win-Back Specialist brings former members back through relationships, not pressure. This is a new role, the first of its kind at DM. You own the entire win-back pipeline and build the function from the ground up.

The opportunity

  • $500K+ in win-backs closed in the last 3 months, with no one dedicated to it.
  • 2,500+ former members already in the pipeline. They have bought before, so there is no cold prospecting.
  • One owner. You get the whole win-back pipeline, with setter support.

The demand is proven. The role has never existed, so the right person builds it.

What you'll do

  • Own the pipeline. You run the full win-back pipeline, from first touch to close.
  • Build relationships. You nurture former members over the long term and follow up tightly until the timing fits.
  • Solve why they left. You find out what went wrong and fix it, using extra discounts and services where needed to restart them.
  • Close deals. You work mostly self-booked calls with setter support, and pick up overflow renewals when needed.

Target: $150K+ in cash collected per month from month 3, on high-ticket memberships (about $10K+ deals).

Webinars: a win-back webinar runs every 2 months to help close the people you have been talking to.

Requirements

What You Bring

    • A high-ticket track record. You have closed $10K+ deals.
    • Patience with long cycles. You keep relationships warm for months.
    • CRM discipline. You keep clear notes and next steps, and you follow up on time.
    • A consultative approach. You diagnose the problem first, then solve it.
    • Self-starter drive. You book your own meetings and thrive working remotely.
  • This is not a fit if you rely on a high-pressure, one-call-close style, need meetings handed to you or instant wins, are loose with notes and next steps, pitch before understanding the problem, or come from a front-end or appointment-setter background only.
  • Nice to have: renewals, account management or retention experience. No digital assets experience needed.

Benefits

What We Offer

  • Competitive commission structure with bonuses.
  • Full-time, 40 hours a week, with a flexible schedule and unlimited PTO.
  • Entirely remote, working from anywhere in the world, with team off-sites.
  • A supportive, dynamic culture with team members across 30+ countries.

How we hire

  1. Recruiter screen: must-haves, comfort with commission-only pay, long-cycle mindset.
  2. Interview with Renewals Manager: track record and how you nurture a book.
  3. Role play: a mock win-back call with an unhappy ex-member.
  4. Decision: offer and start date.

Job Description

Social Creative & Production Manager

As the Social Creative Manager at Zendesk, you'll help define what great social-first creative looks like for a global technology brand.

We're looking for a creative thinker and hands-on maker who knows how to turn big ideas, complex technology, and timely conversations into content people actually want to engage with. From scroll-stopping videos and bold visual concepts to clever social campaigns and executive content, you'll bring fresh creative thinking to how Zendesk shows up across LinkedIn, X, YouTube, and emerging platforms.


You will turn company priorities, customer stories, product news, thought leadership content, and industry conversations into sharp, platform-native content that earns attention and builds credibility with AI decision-makers and other audiences. You will work closely with brand, product marketing, sales, and PR teams to ensure a consistent, compelling, and integrated brand voice across all social touchpoints, driving measurable impact on our B2B growth objectives. You are a creative, resourceful maker with strong editorial judgment, hands-on production skills, and the instincts to recognize when a moment is worth responding to.


AI fluency is important, too. We're looking for someone who is excited to experiment with emerging creative tools to make production smarter and unlock new possibilities, without sacrificing originality, authenticity, or editorial judgment.


About the Team

This role is part of Zendesk’s brand and content organization and works in close partnership with brand, editorial, product marketing, customer marketing,field marketing, PR and executive communications. The team combines creativity, audience insight, and cross-functional collaboration to strengthen Zendesk’s public presence and support business priorities. This role focuses on producing social content for both Zendesk and its executives.


Here’s What You’ll Do Day-to-day

Concepting & Production

  • Lead ideation and hands-on production of original, social-first content across Zendesk's owned channels, primarily LinkedIn, X, and YouTube.

  • Adapt larger brand campaigns into creative that feels native to each social platform rather than simply resizing existing assets.
  • Partner with internal designers, video producers, and external creative resources on more complex production needs.

Social-First Storytelling & Innovation

  • Bring a strong understanding of social culture, platform trends, emerging formats, and audience behavior to the creative process.
  • Proactively pitch fresh, unexpected ideas that help Zendesk stand out from traditional B2B technology brands.
  • Identify opportunities for timely, relevant, and culturally aware creative that connects Zendesk to broader industry conversations.
  • Experiment with new formats, visual approaches, and storytelling techniques to continuously evolve our social presence.
  • Explore and apply AI-powered creative tools across design, video, ideation, and production while maintaining strong creative judgment and quality standards.

Executive & Thought Leadership Social Content

  • Develop creative concepts and assets supporting Zendesk's executive social presence.
  • Translate executive perspectives, industry insights, and thought leadership into compelling visual and multimedia content.
  • Support executive video content, including creative concepts, scripts, editing, and repurposing longer-form conversations into engaging social clips.

Creative Collaboration & Execution

  • Collaborate with the Senior Social Media & Influencer Manager to translate social strategy and business priorities into creative concepts and deliverables.
  • Partner with Brand, Product Marketing, PR, Communications, and other stakeholders to develop and execute social creative for launches, campaigns, and events.
  • Own assigned creative projects from brief through production, feedback, approvals, and final delivery.
  • Manage creative timelines and deliverables, balancing planned initiatives with timely content opportunities.
  • Work with the broader social team to ensure creative aligns with publishing schedules, platform best practices, and audience needs.
  • Use social performance insights, creative testing, and audience feedback to continually refine and improve content.

Here’s What We’re Looking For

  • 7+ years of overall marketing, communications, journalism, or content experience, with at least 5 years focused on social media or digital content.
  • Proven experience building social content for a B2B, technology, AI,SaaS, or similarly complex brand.
  • A strong portfolio demonstrating excellent social writing and hands-on creation of graphics, carousels, and short-form video.
  • Strong command of design and video editing tools, such as Canva, Adobe Creative Cloud, or equivalent.
  • Exceptional writing, editing, and storytelling skills, including the ability to adapt voice and format for different executives, audiences, and platforms.
  • Experience developing executive social content or thought leadership, with the judgment to make it sound credible and personal.

What Success Looks Like

If you are the kind of person who has always wanted to make a difference and be heard at work, Wagepoint will give you plenty of opportunity to do just that.

The Role at High Level:

We’re looking for a talented People Operations Coordinator who enjoys tackling hard problems and wants to create meaningful impact for small businesses across Canada. You'll keep People Operations running day to day, own onboarding from pre-boarding through a new hire's first 90 days, turn our people data into useful insight, and lead the automation of our People Ops workflows and reporting. You will report directly to our People Operations Manager & People Business Partner.

  • Own the automation of People Ops workflows and reporting with IT, starting with the tasks that repeat most and take the most time, and track the hours you save.

  • Compile, analyze, and spot patterns in the data and bring them to People Ops leadership so plans rest on facts.

EverPro brings together purpose-built tools across key trades - including field service, remodelling and roofing, landscaping, and pest and lawn - so service professionals can manage operations, engage customers, and drive long-term growth.

jobs.description:
About ALC
A la Carte Solutions (ALC) is an Inc. 5000 firm. We provide outsourced finance, accounting and HR services to about 80 businesses across the US. Our brand promise is Wow Professionally, Care Personally, and it shapes how we treat clients and each other.

The Role
ALC built its own operating platform, ALC PACE. It has already replaced several third-party tools and is on its way to being the one system our team uses to run the firm. We’re looking for a senior, hands-on builder to own it.

You’ll architect, write, review and ship code every day. You’ll use Claude Code and similar AI tools heavily, and you’ll own the quality of what they produce. You’ll also lead the build of ALC’s first products for clients: a client portal, plus AI agents and automations for client workflows.

This isn’t a ticket-taking job. It’s for someone at manager-to-director level who still wants to build. You’ll sit with the people who use the platform, learn how the business works, and build what actually moves it forward. As the platform grows, you’ll set the standards, documentation and release process that let it scale, and eventually let a team build on it.

This is a fully remote role for candidates based in Latin America. You’ll work in your local time zone. You’ll also need the flexibility to join meetings and support colleagues in the US and other time zones when the work calls for it. All work is in English.

Our Stack
ALC PACE · GitHub · Railway · Neon (Postgres) · Claude Code · HubSpot (migrating into PACE) · third-party APIs

What You’ll Do: Wow Professionally

  • Own the architecture: Turn PACE into one connected system. Reporting, time review, billing, CRM, client operations and HR workflows should all share a single Postgres data model.
  • Build and ship every day: Own features end to end, from the first conversation with a stakeholder through build, deployment and support. Ship through a clean, repeatable release process.
  • Replace outside tools with PACE: Lead the move of our HubSpot CRM into PACE, redesigning the process rather than copying the old tool. Recommend which tools to replace next.
  • Turn spreadsheets into apps: Convert Excel models (capacity planning, direct margin, client profitability) into live features.
  • Build client-facing products: Help build the client portal. Design multi-tenant permissions that keep each client’s data secure and separate.
  • Build AI agents and automations: Design, build and evaluate agents and automations for internal and client workflows, including tool use, retrieval, prompt design and evaluation.
  • Own the quality of AI-written code: Review AI output like a draft from a talented junior engineer. Catch logic errors, security gaps and data-integrity problems before users see them.
  • Document everything: Write architecture, data model and runbook docs so the platform doesn’t depend on any one person’s knowledge.

How You’ll Show Up: Care Personally

  • Partner with stakeholders: Sit with leadership and department heads, ask good questions, and turn how they work into clear requirements. Push back respectfully when a request wouldn’t serve the bigger system.
  • Build with the business in mind: Know whether a feature saves time, improves margin or makes a client’s life easier, and prioritize accordingly.
  • Speak plainly: Explain technical tradeoffs and write updates that non-engineers can follow.
  • Drive adoption, not just delivery: Support the team through changes like the HubSpot migration so new tools actually get used.

What Success Looks Like

  • 30 days: You’re set up locally, you know the architecture and data model, and you’ve shipped your first fixes to production.
  • 90 days: You’ve owned a meaningful feature end to end and written a prioritized plan for risk and technical debt.
  • 180 days: You’re the go-to owner for major parts of the platform. You’ve led a spreadsheet-to-app or HubSpot migration workstream, contributed to the client portal, and set standards others can build on.

Requirements

You Bring

  • A track record of real, shipped work. A degree isn’t required.
  • 7+ years building and shipping web applications, including owning production systems end to end.
  • Experience as a technical lead or architect: setting standards, reviewing code and owning a platform or product area.
  • Fluency in a modern web stack: JavaScript/TypeScript, React or similar, and Node or Python.
  • Strong SQL and data modeling, with Postgres preferred.
  • Hands-on integration work with REST APIs, webhooks and authentication flows.
  • Daily use of AI coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot or similar), with examples of catching their mistakes.
  • Solid Git workflow and production deployment experience on a cloud platform.
  • Professional English, strong enough to lead stakeholder meetings and write documentation for non-technical colleagues.
  • Flexibility to work across time zones, including regular overlap with US-based colleagues.

Nice to Have

  • Experience building AI agents or LLM-powered workflows
  • Experience replacing SaaS products with custom software, or building internal tools or ERPs
  • Experience migrating HubSpot or other CRM data
  • Exposure to finance, accounting, HR or professional services operations
  • Experience building multi-tenant client portals
  • Experience with Railway, Neon or similar platforms

How You Think
You’re a systems thinker: before you build, you ask where the data comes from, where it goes and what else it touches. You can take a loosely defined problem, scope it and ship something useful. You move fast with AI tools without trusting them blindly.

Benefits

  • Pay: $5,000 – $6,500 USD per month ($60,000 – $78,000 USD per year), depending on experience
  • Full-time employment through our employer-of-record partner, including statutory benefits required in your country
  • Flexible PTO with no set maximum. If you take fewer than 10 days a year, we’ll nudge you to take more.
  • All ALC company holidays off
  • Fully remote, working in your local time zone
  • A chance to build a platform from the ground up at a growing Inc. 5000 firm
  • Direct work with ALC’s leadership team and a real say in the product

jobs.title: Group Chief Procurement Officer (Group CPO) – Insurance & Investment
jobs.description:
Group Chief Procurement Officer (Group CPO) – Insurance & Investments

1. Role Summary

The Group Chief Procurement Officer (Group CPO) is responsible for developing, leading and executing the group-wide procurement, strategic sourcing and supplier management strategy across all subsidiaries, business units, operating entities and geographical markets within the organization.

The role provides strategic leadership over procurement governance, commercial negotiations, vendor relationships, cost optimization, third-party risk management, procurement operations and sourcing transformation. The Group CPO ensures procurement activities support the organization's financial performance, operational efficiency, regulatory compliance, business continuity and strategic objectives.

Within an Insurance & Investments group, the role oversees procurement of technology, insurance operations, investment-related services, professional services, outsourcing, facilities, corporate services and other strategic goods and services.

2. Key Responsibilities

A. Group Procurement Strategy & Leadership

  • Develop and implement the group-wide procurement strategy aligned with corporate objectives, financial targets and business priorities.
  • Establish procurement policies, frameworks, standards and operating models across subsidiaries and business units.
  • Lead centralized, decentralized or hybrid procurement structures to optimize group-wide purchasing activities.
  • Drive procurement maturity, operational efficiency and strategic sourcing capability across the organization.
  • Advise executive leadership and the board on procurement strategy, commercial opportunities and supplier-related risks.

B. Strategic Sourcing & Category Management

  • Lead strategic sourcing initiatives across major procurement categories, including IT, insurance operations, investment services, consulting, outsourcing, facilities and corporate services.
  • Develop category strategies, sourcing plans, supplier selection frameworks and procurement roadmaps.
  • Oversee competitive bidding, RFPs, RFQs, tendering, vendor evaluations and contract award processes.
  • Identify opportunities for group-wide procurement consolidation, economies of scale and supplier rationalization.
  • Drive strategic negotiations to secure commercial value, quality, service delivery and contractual protection.

C. Supplier & Vendor Management

  • Establish and oversee strategic supplier relationship management frameworks across the group.
  • Manage relationships with key suppliers, strategic partners, technology providers, outsourcing partners and service providers.
  • Develop supplier performance management frameworks, service-level agreements (SLAs), scorecards and review mechanisms.
  • Monitor supplier delivery, service quality, financial stability, contractual obligations and operational performance.
  • Lead supplier escalation, renegotiation, remediation and relationship improvement initiatives.

D. Cost Optimization & Financial Management

  • Drive procurement-led savings, cost optimization, cost avoidance and financial efficiency across group operations.
  • Develop procurement budgets, savings targets, spend forecasts and financial reporting frameworks.
  • Identify opportunities to optimize operating expenditure (OPEX), capital expenditure (CAPEX) and vendor spending.
  • Collaborate with Finance, business leaders and subsidiary management to validate procurement savings and benefits realization.
  • Monitor procurement spend, budget performance, financial controls and cost reduction initiatives.

E. Contract & Commercial Management

  • Lead complex commercial negotiations, strategic contract agreements, supplier terms and procurement-related commitments.
  • Establish group-wide contract management standards, renewal controls and commercial governance.
  • Ensure contracts reflect pricing, performance requirements, service levels, risk allocation, termination provisions and business continuity obligations.
  • Partner with Legal, Finance, Risk and Compliance teams on contract review, commercial risk and regulatory obligations.
  • Monitor contract lifecycle management, renewals, variations, disputes and contractual performance.

F. Procurement Governance, Risk & Compliance

  • Establish procurement governance frameworks, delegated authority structures, approval processes and procurement controls.
  • Ensure procurement practices comply with regulatory requirements, internal policies, ethical standards and corporate governance.
  • Oversee supplier due diligence, procurement risk assessments, conflict-of-interest controls and supplier integrity checks.
  • Collaborate with Risk, Compliance, Internal Audit and Legal teams to manage procurement-related risks.
  • Ensure procurement transparency, audit readiness, accountability and responsible purchasing practices.

G. Third-Party Risk & Outsourcing Management

  • Lead group-level oversight of third-party relationships, outsourced services and strategic vendor dependencies.
  • Ensure supplier risk assessment, due diligence, onboarding, monitoring and exit management processes are implemented.
  • Manage third-party operational, cybersecurity, data privacy, financial, reputational and business continuity risks.
  • Oversee critical supplier and outsourcing arrangements relevant to insurance and investment operations.
  • Ensure third-party governance aligns with the organization's risk management framework and applicable regulatory expectations.

H. Procurement Transformation & Digitalization

  • Drive procurement transformation initiatives to improve sourcing efficiency, automation, analytics and process standardization.
  • Implement or oversee procurement technology, e-procurement, spend analytics, contract management and supplier management platforms.
  • Leverage data analytics and technology to improve procurement visibility, forecasting, supplier performance and decision-making.
  • Lead process redesign, procurement operating model transformation and digital procurement adoption.
  • Promote continuous improvement, innovation and best practices across the group procurement function.

I. Executive Stakeholder & Business Partnership

  • Partner with Group CEO, COO, CFO, CIO, business unit leaders and subsidiary executives on procurement priorities.
  • Align procurement strategies with business growth, transformation, investment, operational and organizational priorities.
  • Provide executive-level procurement insights, recommendations, performance reports and strategic analysis.
  • Influence senior stakeholders on sourcing decisions, supplier strategy, commercial risk and cost optimization.
  • Build strong cross-functional relationships to ensure procurement delivers business value.

J. Team Leadership & Organizational Development

  • Lead, develop and oversee group procurement, strategic sourcing, category management and vendor management teams.
  • Establish organizational structures, talent development plans, performance expectations and succession strategies.
  • Promote procurement excellence, ethical conduct, accountability, collaboration and commercial awareness.
  • Build procurement capability across subsidiaries, business units and regional operations.
  • Drive leadership development, performance management and continuous professional development.

3. Required Qualifications & Experience

Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Procurement, Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, Finance, Economics or a related discipline.
  • Master's degree in Business Administration (MBA), Supply Chain Management, Procurement or Strategic Management preferred.
  • Professional certifications such as CIPS, CPSM, MCIPS or equivalent procurement qualifications are highly desirable.

Professional Experience

  • 12–18+ years of progressive procurement, sourcing, commercial or supply chain experience.
  • Significant experience in senior procurement leadership, preferably at Director, VP or C-suite level.
  • Proven experience leading group-wide, multi-entity, multinational or multi-business procurement functions.
  • Strong experience in strategic sourcing, category management, contract negotiation and supplier management.
  • Demonstrated track record of delivering measurable cost savings, procurement transformation and commercial value.
  • Experience managing procurement across complex organizations, regulated industries or financial services environments.
  • Experience in third-party risk management, outsourcing governance and supplier performance management.
  • Exposure to insurance, investment management, banking, financial services or other highly regulated industries is preferred.

Technical & Leadership Competencies

  • Group-wide procurement strategy and governance.
  • Strategic sourcing and category management.
  • Commercial negotiation and contract management.
  • Supplier relationship and vendor management.
  • Spend analytics and financial management.
  • Third-party risk and outsourcing oversight.
  • Procurement transformation and digitalization.
  • Regulatory compliance and corporate governance.

- Executive stakeholder management.

We exist to create positive change for people and the planet. Join us and make a difference too!

Head of Artificial Intelligence Global Quality & Accreditation

Location: Global Homebased, travel required

About the role

We have an exciting opportunity become available for the Head of AI Global Quality & Accreditation. The purpose of this role will be to:

  • Lead BSI’s efforts in Developing Conformity Assessment Activity to allow manufacturers and providers to demonstrate that their technology conforms to the provisions of the evolving EU AI Regulations
  • Be the ambassador representing BSI as a global leader in key AI Technical Forums in Europe and Globally as an industry leading expert regulator.
  • Ensure that NB personnel work consistently at the required high level of expertise and rigour
  • Ensure that BSI has the relevant policies, procedures and documentation are in place to meet all AI regulatory obligations
  • Work with the GRC team on competence qualifications, personal development and certificate decision making. This responsibility will involve the application of personal authority and expertise rather than hierarchical position.
  • Shape & define BSI Group business plan for AI and Machine Learning in the regulatory space, working alongside Marketing and the innovations Team to identify and quantify opportunities in high risk areas with mandated regulation.
  • Possible Focus areas may include:
  • Medical Devices / In vitro Diagnostic Devices
  • Real time/remote biometric identification
  • Equipment and protective systems for use in explosive atmospheres
  • Radio equipment
  • Pressure equipment
  • Appliances burning gaseous fuels
  • Road traffic, supply of water, gas, heating, and electricity

Key responsibilities:

  • Lead the Designation activity to obtain AI Notified Body Status within the EU in the targeted areas and lead on regulatory issues, both internal and external.
  • Lead the development and implementation of the necessary processes and procedures that enable staff to comply with the EU AI Regulation and associated Notified Body designation and accreditation requirements.
  • Work with the GRC Professional Development team to establish qualification criteria for all roles.
  • Lead your team to ensure staff comply with the new AI NB’s processes and procedures working with the GRC Professional Development group.
  • Lead your team in providing expert regulatory support for the wider team (Group) and to customers.
  • Mentor and Support NL Team with Designating Authority (TBC).
  • Support the UK Approved Body and other International Regulatory programs.
  • Identify the opportunities for business process improvement.
  • Keep the Certification Process output consistent working with C&R, Operations, and Professional Development to support all operational teams.

To be successful in the role you will have:

  • BSc degree in discipline relevant to AI and or from a target industry sector. Postgraduate qualification in AI & or Machine learning Technology and or a Regulatory Affairs background would be advantageous.
  • Thorough knowledge of existing and proposed AI regulations worldwide and particularly the EU AI regulatory approach.
  • Knowledge of business processes and the application of quality management standards
  • A team player good at relationship building internally and externally
  • Broad technical understanding of focal area industry products
  • Conceptual and analytical thinking, efficiency, and results orientation
  • General knowledge of business principles and operating practices (commercial awareness)
  • Ability to understand and interpret legislation and input to policy
  • People leadership / influencing skills
  • Good interpersonal skills, particularly communication and influencing skills
  • Capable of operating with horizontal and vertical reporting lines

BSI offers a competitive total reward package, an independent and varied job in an international environment, flexible working hours, ongoing training and development.

The salary for Netherlands can range from €96,000-120,000 annually; actual compensation is based on various factors, including but not limited to, the candidate’s competencies, level of experience, education, location, divisional budget and internal peer compensation comparisons. As this role can be based homebased globally across EMEA your recruiter can advise of salary for the country you are based.

About Us

BSI is a business improvement and standards company and for over a century BSI has been recognized for having a positive impact on organizations and society, building trust and enhancing lives.

Today BSI partners with more than 77,500 clients in 195 countries and engages with a 15,000 strong global community of experts, industry and consumer groups, organizations and governments.
Utilizing its extensive expertise in key industry sectors - including automotive, aerospace, built environment, food and retail, and healthcare - BSI delivers on its purpose by helping its clients fulfil theirs.
Living by our core values of Client-Centricity, Agility, and Collaboration, BSI provides organizations with the confidence to grow by partnering with them to tackle society’s critical issues – from climate change to building trust in digital transformation and everything in between - to accelerate progress towards a better society and a sustainable world.

BSI is an Equal Opportunity Employer dedicated to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace.

jobs.title: Group Chief Procurement Officer (Group CPO) – Insurance & Investment
jobs.description:
Group Chief Procurement Officer (Group CPO) – Insurance & Investments

1. Role Summary

The Group Chief Procurement Officer (Group CPO) is responsible for developing, leading and executing the group-wide procurement, strategic sourcing and supplier management strategy across all subsidiaries, business units, operating entities and geographical markets within the organization.

The role provides strategic leadership over procurement governance, commercial negotiations, vendor relationships, cost optimization, third-party risk management, procurement operations and sourcing transformation. The Group CPO ensures procurement activities support the organization's financial performance, operational efficiency, regulatory compliance, business continuity and strategic objectives.

Within an Insurance & Investments group, the role oversees procurement of technology, insurance operations, investment-related services, professional services, outsourcing, facilities, corporate services and other strategic goods and services.

2. Key Responsibilities

A. Group Procurement Strategy & Leadership

  • Develop and implement the group-wide procurement strategy aligned with corporate objectives, financial targets and business priorities.
  • Establish procurement policies, frameworks, standards and operating models across subsidiaries and business units.
  • Lead centralized, decentralized or hybrid procurement structures to optimize group-wide purchasing activities.
  • Drive procurement maturity, operational efficiency and strategic sourcing capability across the organization.
  • Advise executive leadership and the board on procurement strategy, commercial opportunities and supplier-related risks.

B. Strategic Sourcing & Category Management

  • Lead strategic sourcing initiatives across major procurement categories, including IT, insurance operations, investment services, consulting, outsourcing, facilities and corporate services.
  • Develop category strategies, sourcing plans, supplier selection frameworks and procurement roadmaps.
  • Oversee competitive bidding, RFPs, RFQs, tendering, vendor evaluations and contract award processes.
  • Identify opportunities for group-wide procurement consolidation, economies of scale and supplier rationalization.
  • Drive strategic negotiations to secure commercial value, quality, service delivery and contractual protection.

C. Supplier & Vendor Management

  • Establish and oversee strategic supplier relationship management frameworks across the group.
  • Manage relationships with key suppliers, strategic partners, technology providers, outsourcing partners and service providers.
  • Develop supplier performance management frameworks, service-level agreements (SLAs), scorecards and review mechanisms.
  • Monitor supplier delivery, service quality, financial stability, contractual obligations and operational performance.
  • Lead supplier escalation, renegotiation, remediation and relationship improvement initiatives.

D. Cost Optimization & Financial Management

  • Drive procurement-led savings, cost optimization, cost avoidance and financial efficiency across group operations.
  • Develop procurement budgets, savings targets, spend forecasts and financial reporting frameworks.
  • Identify opportunities to optimize operating expenditure (OPEX), capital expenditure (CAPEX) and vendor spending.
  • Collaborate with Finance, business leaders and subsidiary management to validate procurement savings and benefits realization.
  • Monitor procurement spend, budget performance, financial controls and cost reduction initiatives.

E. Contract & Commercial Management

  • Lead complex commercial negotiations, strategic contract agreements, supplier terms and procurement-related commitments.
  • Establish group-wide contract management standards, renewal controls and commercial governance.
  • Ensure contracts reflect pricing, performance requirements, service levels, risk allocation, termination provisions and business continuity obligations.
  • Partner with Legal, Finance, Risk and Compliance teams on contract review, commercial risk and regulatory obligations.
  • Monitor contract lifecycle management, renewals, variations, disputes and contractual performance.

F. Procurement Governance, Risk & Compliance

  • Establish procurement governance frameworks, delegated authority structures, approval processes and procurement controls.
  • Ensure procurement practices comply with regulatory requirements, internal policies, ethical standards and corporate governance.
  • Oversee supplier due diligence, procurement risk assessments, conflict-of-interest controls and supplier integrity checks.
  • Collaborate with Risk, Compliance, Internal Audit and Legal teams to manage procurement-related risks.
  • Ensure procurement transparency, audit readiness, accountability and responsible purchasing practices.

G. Third-Party Risk & Outsourcing Management

  • Lead group-level oversight of third-party relationships, outsourced services and strategic vendor dependencies.
  • Ensure supplier risk assessment, due diligence, onboarding, monitoring and exit management processes are implemented.
  • Manage third-party operational, cybersecurity, data privacy, financial, reputational and business continuity risks.
  • Oversee critical supplier and outsourcing arrangements relevant to insurance and investment operations.
  • Ensure third-party governance aligns with the organization's risk management framework and applicable regulatory expectations.

H. Procurement Transformation & Digitalization

  • Drive procurement transformation initiatives to improve sourcing efficiency, automation, analytics and process standardization.
  • Implement or oversee procurement technology, e-procurement, spend analytics, contract management and supplier management platforms.
  • Leverage data analytics and technology to improve procurement visibility, forecasting, supplier performance and decision-making.
  • Lead process redesign, procurement operating model transformation and digital procurement adoption.
  • Promote continuous improvement, innovation and best practices across the group procurement function.

I. Executive Stakeholder & Business Partnership

  • Partner with Group CEO, COO, CFO, CIO, business unit leaders and subsidiary executives on procurement priorities.
  • Align procurement strategies with business growth, transformation, investment, operational and organizational priorities.
  • Provide executive-level procurement insights, recommendations, performance reports and strategic analysis.
  • Influence senior stakeholders on sourcing decisions, supplier strategy, commercial risk and cost optimization.
  • Build strong cross-functional relationships to ensure procurement delivers business value.

J. Team Leadership & Organizational Development

  • Lead, develop and oversee group procurement, strategic sourcing, category management and vendor management teams.
  • Establish organizational structures, talent development plans, performance expectations and succession strategies.
  • Promote procurement excellence, ethical conduct, accountability, collaboration and commercial awareness.
  • Build procurement capability across subsidiaries, business units and regional operations.
  • Drive leadership development, performance management and continuous professional development.

3. Required Qualifications & Experience

Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Procurement, Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, Finance, Economics or a related discipline.
  • Master's degree in Business Administration (MBA), Supply Chain Management, Procurement or Strategic Management preferred.
  • Professional certifications such as CIPS, CPSM, MCIPS or equivalent procurement qualifications are highly desirable.

Professional Experience

  • 12–18+ years of progressive procurement, sourcing, commercial or supply chain experience.
  • Significant experience in senior procurement leadership, preferably at Director, VP or C-suite level.
  • Proven experience leading group-wide, multi-entity, multinational or multi-business procurement functions.
  • Strong experience in strategic sourcing, category management, contract negotiation and supplier management.
  • Demonstrated track record of delivering measurable cost savings, procurement transformation and commercial value.
  • Experience managing procurement across complex organizations, regulated industries or financial services environments.
  • Experience in third-party risk management, outsourcing governance and supplier performance management.
  • Exposure to insurance, investment management, banking, financial services or other highly regulated industries is preferred.

Technical & Leadership Competencies

  • Group-wide procurement strategy and governance.
  • Strategic sourcing and category management.
  • Commercial negotiation and contract management.
  • Supplier relationship and vendor management.
  • Spend analytics and financial management.
  • Third-party risk and outsourcing oversight.
  • Procurement transformation and digitalization.
  • Regulatory compliance and corporate governance.

- Executive stakeholder management.

  • Organizational leadership and team development.

4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

KPI CategoryPerformance Indicators

Cost SavingsProcurement savings, cost avoidance and cost optimization achieved across the group.

Spend ManagementSpend under management, procurement spend visibility and strategic spend coverage.

Sourcing EffectivenessCompetitive sourcing rates, sourcing cycle time and sourcing strategy execution.

Supplier PerformanceSupplier SLA achievement, quality, delivery performance and supplier scorecard results.

Contract ManagementContract compliance, contract coverage, renewal management and negotiated commercial value.

Procurement CompliancePolicy compliance, approval adherence, audit findings and procurement control effectiveness.

Third-Party RiskSupplier risk assessment completion, critical supplier monitoring and risk remediation.

Operational EfficiencyProcurement cycle time, process efficiency and procurement service delivery.

TransformationProcurement technology adoption, automation and process improvement outcomes.

LeadershipProcurement team performance, capability development, stakeholder satisfaction and succession readiness.

jobs.title: Principal Product Manager, Sandboxes
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Canada

About Docker

Docker is the platform at the center of how intelligent software gets built. For more than a decade, Docker has helped millions of developers and thousands of organizations build, ship, and run software consistently across any environment. Today, Docker extends that same trust to the AI era. Docker Hardened Images form the foundation agentic code is built on, local and cloud Docker Sandboxes isolate where agents run, and Docker AI Governance sets enterprise-wide policy. Together, they give builders and organizations the confidence to adopt any model, tool, or agent without compromising security, governance, or control.

_______________________________________________________________________

The Role

The Products Team at Docker is looking for a Principal Product Manager to lead components of Docker Sandboxes. You will own and drive this strategic product area from high-level concept design through delivery, adoption, and operation. You will help shape how developers and AI agents use fast, secure, isolated environments across local and cloud workflows. You will work closely with developers inside and outside of Docker, our customers, and our partners to expand our open ecosystem offering and provide value. As the company and ecosystem grow, you will help foster teams eager to continuously build, measure, and learn.

To thrive in this role, you will need experience working with developers, deep technical fluency in systems and developer infrastructure, and prior experience as a software engineer. You will need to understand containers, sandboxes/microVMs, virtualization technologies, hypervisors, the software development lifecycle, and how untrusted or agent-generated code can be safely executed and orchestrated. You will need a relentless drive to try new things and an eye for detail. Your long-term success will depend on your ability to own the product roadmap, earn the trust of the developer community, and scale reliable services. Most importantly, you will need to be comfortable taking ownership of big objectives with big goals, working with a cross-functional team, and maintaining a bias for action.

_______________________________________________________________________

Responsibilities

  • You own Docker Sandboxes, its long-term vision, roadmap, revenue, adoption, and results.

  • You believe in and can succinctly articulate our customers, their workflows, and their pain points. You empathize with the world they live in and the security, performance, compatibility, and cost constraints they work through.

  • You will engage deeply with developers building AI agents, coding environments, CI and testing systems, and other workloads that require secure, isolated execution, finding solutions for today while optimizing for tomorrow's vision.

  • You enjoy building infrastructure products that are easy to adopt and use. You will turn complex tradeoffs across isolation, startup time, performance, density, networking, storage, and cost into simple product experiences.

  • You are comfortable with ambiguity and will guide product definition, feature prioritization, and scope in concert with engineering, design, security, operations, and go-to-market teams.

  • You are a fan of iterative development, working with customers and cross-functional teams to hypothesize, measure adoption and impact, learn from releases, and continually improve the roadmap.

_______________________________________________________________________

Qualifications

  • You have deep empathy for the needs of developers and are obsessed with talking to your users.

  • You have prior professional experience as a software engineer, ideally in systems, infrastructure, platform engineering, developer tools, or cloud.

  • You have strong technical familiarity with sandboxes/microVMs, containers, virtualization technologies, and hypervisors, including the isolation and security boundaries each provides.

  • You understand the building blocks of modern developer infrastructure, including Linux, container runtimes, orchestration, networking, storage, APIs, and cloud services.

  • You have experience designing, building, or operating systems that execute customer-provided, untrusted, or agent-generated code at scale.

  • You are comfortable interacting with a command-line interface and discussing APIs, SDKs, and technical architecture with engineers and developers.

  • You have experience building B2B or SaaS products, or a background in public cloud and developer infrastructure.

  • You understand software supply chain and software security concerns, including multi-tenant isolation, identity, secrets management, observability, and reliability.

  • You can break down complex technical problems into small, releasable, user-valuable features.

  • You can explain complex ideas simply and communicate effectively in writing, verbally, and visually across diverse stakeholders.

  • You can analyze qualitative and quantitative data to inform decisions, define success metrics, and prioritize investments.

  • You have a collaborative approach, experience running products from greenfield to scale, and the ability to work with fast-moving, distributed, cross-functional teams. You are a doer as well as a strategist; we are small and need all hands on deck.

_______________________________________________________________________

What to expect
First 30 days

  • Get to know Docker: our vision, mission, and values.

  • Understand the Docker Sandboxes team's mission, product strategy, and technical architecture.

  • Meet the team along with peers across the business unit and company.

  • Work closely with designers, researchers, engineers, security partners, and customers to understand user needs and current pain points.

  • Work with your manager and team to review and create quarterly goals.

  • Understand the product roadmap, key technical and business tradeoffs, and the data available to make data-driven decisions.

First 90 days

  • Understand the company's and business unit's product vision and how Docker Sandboxes contributes to it.

  • Provide clarity on product vision, target users, priority use cases, and how the team contributes to the overall success of Docker.

  • Develop a deep understanding of our developers and customers, how they use isolated environments, and why they choose Docker.

  • Shape the team roadmap and product strategy in close collaboration with design, engineering, security, and go-to-market peers.

  • Lead the definition of team OKRs and success metrics for the quarter, and provide clear progress reports.

One Year Outlook

  • Lead product initiatives across cross-functional teams that make secure, isolated execution simple and valuable for developers and AI agents.

  • Drive the long-term direction of Docker Sandboxes, including improvements to adoption, ecosystem integration, reliability, scale, unit economics, and ARR.

Visa sponsorship: Not available for this role.

_______________________________________________________________________

Compensation & Equity

All full-time roles include equity. Final compensation is determined on factors including but not limited to experience, skills, qualifications, and location.

Canada CA$255,500 - CA$365,000 base

United States: $280,000 – $300,000 base

______________________________________________________________________

Posting Information

  • Open vacancy: This posting is for an existing open role.

  • AI in hiring: Docker may use AI-assisted tools during our recruiting process.

  • Interview recordings: Candidates will be invited to opt in to interview recordings to support interviewer calibration and consistent evaluations. Recordings are optional and require explicit consent.

______________________________________________________________________

Perks & Benefits

  • Remote-first by design – Work from your home, with offices in Seattle and Paris for connection and collaboration.

  • Flexibility that fits your life – We trust you to manage your schedule while delivering great work.

  • Time to recharge – Generous PTO, designated quarterly Whaleness Days, and a designated end-of-year Whaleness break.

  • Home office support – Set up your workspace for comfort and success.

  • Technology stipend – Equivalent to US$100 net per month to help support your work.

  • Learning & development – Annual stipend for conferences, courses, certifications, and continued learning.

  • Parental leave – 16 weeks of paid parental leave after six months of employment.

  • Equity for all full-time employees – Share in Docker's long-term success as we continue to grow.

  • Comprehensive benefits – Medical, retirement, and paid holidays vary by country.

  • Docker swag – Because representing the whale never gets old.

Docker is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a team that reflects a broad range of backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe diverse teams build better products, make better decisions, and better serve our global community.

jobs.title: Head of Payments & Payment Strategy
jobs.description:
We are looking for a Head of Payments who has run payments from the merchant's seat. You have owned checkout, billing and fraud for a global online business, and you were accountable for the revenue those decisions produced.

You will own how our customers pay in every market we sell in: what the payment page looks like, which methods and currencies it offers by region, how transactions are routed and retried, and where we set the line on fraud. Success is measured in checkout conversion, approval rates, recovered revenue, fraud losses and cost per transaction.

This is a hands-on operating role. You will be in the data every day, finding where approvals drop or customers abandon, and fixing it with Product, Engineering, Finance and Risk.
You will work closely with CentroBill, our internal billing and acquiring arm. CentroBill provides the gateway, acquiring relationships and payment method coverage. You are its merchant-side counterpart: you set the requirements, review performance together and push for the routing, coverage and commercial terms the business needs.

About Us

Centro is an international product company with over 20 years of expertise in product development, affiliate marketing and online technologies. Our team of 300+ professionals across Europe and North America builds products used by millions of users worldwide.

What You Will Manage Daily

  • Checkout conversion by market, device, traffic source and product, from payment page load to successful charge.
  • Approval and decline rates by region, acquirer, card type and issuer, split by initial sales, trial conversions, upsells and renewals.
  • Decline reason codes, and the routing, cascading and retry rules that respond to them.
  • Payment method and currency mix in each region, so customers see the options they trust and expect locally.
  • Fraud rules and 3DS settings, watching false declines as closely as fraud losses.
  • Chargebacks, pre-dispute alerts and refunds, tracked against card scheme monitoring thresholds.
  • Recurring billing health: renewal success, failed rebills, retry schedules and involuntary churn.
  • CentroBill and provider performance: uptime, incidents, cost and the fallback when something underperforms.

Key Responsibilities

Checkout and payment page optimization

  • Own the payment page experience across web and mobile: layout, form fields, method ordering, error messaging and localization.
  • Add and tune express checkout options such as Apple Pay and Google Pay where they lift conversion.
  • Run a continuous testing program on checkout flows and report results in conversion and revenue terms.
  • Work with Product and Engineering to prioritize and ship checkout and billing improvements.

Regional payment strategy

  • Decide which cards, wallets, bank transfers and local payment methods to offer in each market, based on customer behavior and unit economics.
  • Set currency, pricing presentation and local acquiring strategy by region to lift approval rates and reduce cross-border costs.
  • Launch payments in new markets and retire methods that do not earn their place.

Authorization and revenue optimization

  • Drive improvements in authorization rates, payment conversion and transaction success rates.
  • Own payment routing, cascading and retry logic across providers.
  • Identify revenue leakage and fix it: soft declines, failed renewals, abandoned payments and avoidable fees.

Subscription and recurring billing

  • Improve trial-to-paid conversion and renewal success rates.
  • Optimize rebill timing, retry schedules, card updater and network token usage, and dunning communication.
  • Reduce involuntary churn and raise payment recovery rates.

Fraud, risk and chargebacks

  • Set fraud rules and 3DS strategy by region, balancing acceptance, fraud exposure and customer experience.
  • Oversee chargeback prevention, pre-dispute alerts, dispute handling and win rates with Risk and Compliance.
  • Keep dispute and fraud ratios within card scheme monitoring program thresholds across every merchant account.
  • Keep checkout and billing flows compliant with card scheme rules, PCI DSS and PSD2.

CentroBill partnership and provider management

  • Act as the business's primary partner to CentroBill, our internal billing and acquiring arm, representing merchant-side needs in its roadmap and priorities.
  • Source and bring forward new acquirers where they improve coverage, approvals or cost. CentroBill is the primary partner, and you are free to go outside it when another acquirer serves the business better. Work with CentroBill on merchant account structure, routing and payment method coverage in each region.
  • Run regular performance reviews with CentroBill on approvals, declines, chargebacks, uptime and cost, and agree the actions that follow.
  • Select and manage any third-party fraud, dispute and checkout vendors the business uses.
  • Own the merchant-side payment roadmap and total cost of payments.

Leadership and reporting

  • Define payment KPIs, build the dashboards that track them and review performance daily.
  • Build and lead the payments team as the function grows.
  • Partner with Product, Engineering, Finance and Risk on payment initiatives.
  • Bring clear recommendations and trade-offs to senior leadership.

Requirements

  • 8+ years in digital payments, with a substantial part of that spent merchant-side at an international e-commerce, subscription or digital goods business.
  • Direct ownership of checkout and payment page performance, with before-and-after numbers you can walk us through on conversion, approval, renewal or recovery rates.
  • Experience building payment strategy by region: local payment methods, wallets, currencies, local acquiring and regulatory requirements such as SCA and 3DS.
  • Deep understanding of recurring billing, trial and subscription payments, payment recovery, routing and cascading.
  • Hands-on experience setting fraud rules and managing chargebacks, pre-dispute alerts and card scheme monitoring programs, including the trade-off between fraud losses and false declines.
  • Experience sourcing acquirers and running multiple merchant accounts across them, and working with a gateway or acquiring partner as a demanding, constructive merchant.
  • Self-sufficient in data: you pull and analyze transaction-level data yourself and turn findings into measurable results.
  • Experience with high-risk industries, subscription-based businesses or complex online merchant environments.
  • Strong commercial judgment and stakeholder management across Product, Engineering, Finance and Risk.

Why Work With Us

  • Competitive salary that reflects your skills and experience.
  • Growth and development, with support for your professional development.
  • High level of autonomy, ownership and accountability.
  • No bureaucracy or micromanagement. We value autonomy and initiative.
  • Educational programs to expand your knowledge and skills.
  • Team-building activities and opportunities to attend industry events.
  • Paid holidays, vacation, personal days and sick leave.
