jobs.title: Environmental Health SME/ Solution Analyst
jobs.description:
About Us

Flourish and Thrive Labs is a woman-owned and led consulting firm specializing in public health solutions. Our team, composed of former public health officials, works with state and local health departments across the country, building resilient public health operating systems. We pride ourselves on being different, holding ourselves to high ethical standards, and taking care of each other.

We view our company as an urban neighborhood—a diverse group of individuals coming together to live and work, embracing the beauty in that diversity. We are a wacky bunch who are intent on spreading joy! (We just mailed out stickers to over 200 local health health professionals because we felt they could use more joy!)

As Salesforce, Microsoft, Snowflake, and AWS partners, we specialize in technology implementation with a strong people focus. We combine this with strategic planning, data analysis, coaching, and facilitation to effectively support local public health department staff.

Our core values are:

  • People First
  • Focus on Capacity Building
  • Belief in Continuous Experimentation
  • By Public Heath; For Public Health
  • We Do What Is Right. Always.

We're seeking passionate, joyful individuals who align with our ethos of being different and making a difference.

WE ARE LOOKING FOR A TEAM MEMBER WITH PUBLIC HEALTH EXPERIENCE (LOCAL/ TRIBAL/ STATE/ FEDERAL).

About Consulting at F&T Labs

If you're new to consulting, we want to help you understand what makes F&T Labs different and why our approach might be perfect for you. We know transitioning from government and non-profit to consulting can be a big step, but we've designed our work environment to blend the best of both worlds.

First, let's talk about how we work. Unlike traditional consulting firms, we hire you for a role, not a specific project. This means you can contribute to various initiatives that match your expertise and interests. Think of it as bringing your public health superpowers to different challenges where they're needed most.

We believe in measuring what matters. While many consulting firms focus on billable hours, we care about the quality and impact of your work. Time sheets don't measure your success with us – it's measured by the meaningful solutions you help create for our clients and their communities.

Yes, we have utilization targets (consulting speak for how much of your time is spent on client work), but we view these as guideposts rather than strict rules. They help us ensure we're making a sustainable impact while maintaining a healthy business. These targets are meant to motivate, not to create stress.

One of the most dynamic aspects of consulting is its natural rhythm. Some weeks might be bustling with activity, while others might be quieter. We embrace these ebbs and flows because they create space for both intense, focused work and time for learning, reflection, and personal growth. This is part of our philosophy that work and life shouldn't be at odds – they should be integrated in a sustainable and energizing way.

At our core, we're built on a simple belief: when our team members flourish, our clients flourish, and ultimately, communities thrive. That's why we've created an environment that supports your growth, values your expertise, and understands that the best solutions come from people who feel empowered and energized by their work.

If you're passionate about public health and excited about the possibility of expanding your impact through consulting, we'd love to talk with you. Your experience in public health is valuable, and we're here to help you apply it in new and meaningful ways.

Notice

No 3rd Party Recruiters. No Phone Calls. We are unable to do informational interviews at this moment. Candidates who call or schedule a "coffee chat" will be considered disqualified.

Solutions Analyst / Business Analyst

WE ARE LOOKING FOR A TEAM MEMBER WITH GOVERNMENT PUBLIC HEALTH EXPERIENCE, IDEALLY IN ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH AT A LOCAL HEALTH DEPARTMENT. IF YOU HAVE THAT EXPERIENCE, PLEASE ENSURE IT IS CLEAR ON YOUR RESUME.

Compensation Note: If a salary range is listed for this position, please note that we will offer at the starting point of the band. We cover 100% of your health insurance!

Role Overview

We're seeking a Solutions Analyst who deeply understands how public health departments work and can translate that understanding into technology solutions that actually fit their needs. This role goes beyond gathering requirements. It requires immersing yourself in the workflows, challenges, and realities of public health practice, then figuring out how technology can make things better.

We're especially interested in candidates who have worked in environmental health programs at a local health department. You know what it's like to manage inspections, track permits, navigate compliance workflows, and juggle the reporting demands that come with environmental health. That firsthand experience will shape how you approach every solution you design.

This is a role for someone who naturally translates needs into action. You're the person who listens to a health department director describe their frustrations and can see the solution taking shape. You're the one who watches staff navigate a clunky process and immediately starts thinking about how it could work better. You take the messy, complex reality of public health operations and turn it into clear direction for a technical team to build against. If you've ever found yourself thinking "I know exactly what they need, I just need to explain it in a way the developers will understand," this role is for you.

You'll work on our PH360 platform and various client initiatives, serving as the critical bridge between what health departments need and what our technical teams build. Your lived experience in governmental public health will help you ask the right questions, spot the real problems behind stated requests, and advocate for solutions that work in the real world.

We're looking for someone who thinks holistically about problems, can synthesize input from multiple stakeholders, and isn't afraid to push back when a proposed solution doesn't quite fit. As a consulting firm, we value candidates who are passionate and eager to dive into the work. While this role focuses on solutions analysis, you may also contribute your unique talents to other firm initiatives.

How You'll Work

You'll join an Agile Release Train (ART) that follows SAFe principles. This means:

  • Program Increment (PI) Planning: You'll participate in quarterly planning sessions, helping shape the roadmap based on your understanding of client needs.
  • Sprint Collaboration: You'll work in two-week sprints with daily standups, regular backlog refinement, and sprint retrospectives.
  • Cross-functional Teams: You'll collaborate closely with developers, architects, and QA analysts to ensure solutions meet the real need.
  • Continuous Discovery: You'll maintain ongoing conversations with clients and stakeholders to refine your understanding of their challenges.

Key Responsibilities

  • Immerse yourself in client workflows to understand how public health staff actually do their work, with particular depth in environmental health programs
  • Identify pain points, inefficiencies, and opportunities that clients may not have articulated
  • Synthesize input from multiple stakeholders into coherent solution recommendations
  • Translate complex public health processes into clear user stories and acceptance criteria
  • Lead discovery sessions and workshops with health department staff
  • Serve as the voice of the client within our technical teams
  • Develop process flows, documentation, and visual aids that communicate the "why" behind solutions
  • Challenge assumptions and push back when proposed solutions don't fit client realities

Experience Required

  • 2+ years working in governmental public health (local, state, federal, or tribal)
  • Demonstrated ability to understand complex systems and workflows
  • Strong facilitation and stakeholder engagement skills
  • Experience translating between technical and non-technical audiences
  • Self-motivated with strong initiative
  • Adaptability in dynamic environments
  • Comfort working with AI tools and large language models

Strongly Preferred

  • Direct experience in environmental health programs at a local health department (e.g., inspections, permitting, compliance, complaint response)

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with agile methodologies
  • Familiarity with user story development and acceptance criteria writing
  • Familiarity with Salesforce or similar platforms
  • Background in process improvement or system implementation
  • Understanding of public health data systems and reporting requirements (e.g., environmental health tracking, inspection databases)
  • Experience with discovery techniques (journey mapping, interviews, observation)

Notice

Must be authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship. Willingness to adhere to our no-drug workplace policy. You must agree to undergo eVerify for employment status at hiring.

No 3rd Party Recruiters. No Phone Calls. We are unable to do informational interviews at this moment. Candidates who call or schedule a "coffee chat" will be disqualified.

At Flourish and Thrive Labs, we believe in the unique value each candidate brings. We encourage applications from diverse backgrounds and experiences, even if you don't meet all listed qualifications.

jobs.description:
About CG Oncology, Inc.

Are you ready to make a difference in the world and become part of our patient-centered team that is focused on Attacking Bladder Cancer for a Better Tomorrow? At CG Oncology, we believe that by having exceptionally talented individuals on our team who share our passion and enjoy working together, we can truly achieve our Vision and Mission to benefit patients around the world.

Every day we are making significant advancements across our multiple pipelines and are growing rapidly to meet the needs of our patients who cannot afford to wait to benefit from our novel immunotherapies. Please review this job posting and our Values and if they resonate with you and are what you expect from your organization and team, then we would like to hear from you.

About the role

The Associate Director, Government Pricing & Gross-to-Net Operations serves as CG Oncology's subject matter expert for U.S. government pricing and reimbursement programs and the operational owner for Gross-to-Net (GTN) forecasting processes. The role leads execution of government pricing operations, GTN forecasting support, compliance, financial reporting, and process optimization. This position partners cross-functionally with Market Access, Finance, Commercial Analytics, Legal, Compliance, Accounting, Supply Chain, Patient Services, Distribution, Medical Affairs, and external vendors to ensure accurate government pricing calculations, compliant reporting, and effective support of commercialization and launch-readiness activities.

As CG Oncology continues to grow and commercialize its oncology portfolio, this role will lead government pricing execution across federal and state programs and serve as the day-to-day operational owner of GTN forecasting, GTN model maintenance, assumption management, variance analysis, and GTN reporting while strengthening operational controls and implementing scalable systems and processes that support long-term organizational growth.

Essential Functions

Government Pricing Operations

  • Lead the execution of government pricing calculations, submissions, and reporting across all applicable federal and state pricing programs, including AMP, Best Price, ASP, Medicaid Drug Rebate Program, 340B, Federal Supply Schedule (FSS), Veterans Affairs (VA), Non-Federal Average Manufacturer Price (NFAMP), Federal Ceiling Price (FCP), Medicare, and other government pricing programs.
  • Ensure timely, accurate, and compliant submission of pricing files while maintaining compliance with CMS, HRSA, VA, and other regulatory requirements.
  • Maintain government pricing methodologies, assumptions, calculation documentation, and supporting procedures.
  • Monitor changes in government pricing regulations, including Inflation Reduction Act (IRA), MFN, guidance, and implement required operational changes.

Gross-to-Net Forecasting, Financial Planning & Commercial Support

  • Lead the day-to-day operation and maintenance of the Gross-to-Net forecasting process, including model maintenance, methodology documentation, assumption management, version control, scenario analyses, and routine forecast updates.
  • Evaluate government pricing and GTN impacts associated with commercial contracting strategies, pricing decisions, channel strategy, patient support programs, distribution arrangements, and business development initiatives.
  • Support commercialization planning, launch readiness, AOP, LRP, quarterly forecast updates, and monthly business reviews by preparing GTN forecast analyses, net revenue impact assessments, and key-driver sensitivities.
  • Own preparation of monthly, quarterly, annual, and long-range GTN forecast updates and supporting analyses for Finance
  • Partner with Business Analytics, own to validate and challenge payer mix, site-of-care mix, channel mix, and analog assumptions used in GTN forecasts.
  • Maintain GTN assumption documentation, assumption registers, decision logs, data-source mapping, version control, and audit-ready forecasting files.
  • Prepare GTN forecast packages, variance analyses, executive summaries, and management reports that communicate key drivers, risks, opportunities, and forecast movements.
  • Coordinate GTN data collection and assumption refresh activities across Business Analytics, Distribution, Patient Services, Contracting, Finance, Accounting, and Market Access.

Compliance, Audit & Risk Management

  • Maintain audit-ready documentation supporting government pricing methodologies and reporting.
  • Lead responses to internal audits, external audits, and government inquiries.
  • Identify pricing discrepancies, investigate root causes, and implement sustainable corrective actions.
  • Strengthen internal controls, governance processes, and compliance monitoring activities to minimize operational risk.

Operational Excellence & Systems

  • Evaluate existing government pricing processes and identify opportunities to improve scalability, efficiency, and accuracy.
  • Support implementation, optimization, and ongoing enhancement of government pricing systems and reporting tools.
  • Partner with IT and external vendors to improve data integration, reporting automation, and operational workflows.
  • Evaluate opportunities to leverage automation and AI-enabled analytics to improve government pricing, GTN forecasting, variance analysis, reporting, and operational decision-making.

Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Serve as the company's government pricing subject matter expert across the organization.
  • Build collaborative partnerships with Market Access, Finance, Commercial, Legal, Compliance, Supply Chain, Medical Affairs, and Executive Leadership.
  • Provide technical guidance to internal stakeholders regarding government pricing regulations and financial implications.
  • Support vendor management activities related to government pricing operations, GTN forecasting tools, data feeds, and software platforms.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Economics, or related discipline required.
  • Minimum 8+ years of progressive pharmaceutical or biotechnology government pricing experience.
  • Experience supporting commercial product launches and launch readiness activities.
  • Experience developing, maintaining, and operating GTN forecasting models, assumptions, accrual analyses, scenario planning, variance analyses, and government rebate calculations.
  • Experience supporting Annual Operating Plan (AOP), Long Range Plan (LRP), quarterly forecast updates, and month-end close processes.
  • Strong understanding of payer mix dynamics, site-of-care economics, specialty distribution, specialty pharmacy / specialty distributor operations, 340B exposure, patient support programs, and government pricing implications.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage complex cross-functional forecasting and operational processes involving Finance, Accounting, Business Analytics, Market Access, Patient Services, Distribution, and external vendors

These benefits are designed to support our team to achieve a healthy balance between work and their personal lives to remain refreshed, engaged, and creating an environment where each person can find a deeper meaning and purpose in their work.

Well-Being Benefits eligibility begins the 1st of the month after hire. While a majority of these benefits are for our US-based workforce, we continue to assess comparable levels of benefits for our international team members that are aligned with country-specific regulations and their national programs offered.

jobs.description:
ELESSAR SYSTEMS INC.

Training. Left of Launch.

POSITION DESCRIPTION

Chief Technology Officer (CTO), Elessar Systems

Join a talented founding team and lead the technical strategy, engineering delivery, and security of an AI-enabled defense training platform built to protect communities and critical infrastructure.

Position Summary

Elessar is hiring a Chief Technology Officer to own the technical strategy, engineering execution, and commercial readiness of Q2 Holodeck™. This is a hands-on executive role for someone who wants to do more than manage backlogs and sit in architecture reviews. You will take a working, sophisticated platform — real-time multiplayer simulation, AI-driven NPC decision agents, deterministic scoring, and automated after-action reporting — and transform it into a secure, supportable, commercially deployed product. You will lead the 12-week commercial release, build the technical team, own the security posture, and set the architecture for the next 24 months of growth.

You will join a small, talented team of technologists, operators, trainers, and business builders. The decisions you make will be visible. Your work will directly determine what Elessar can promise customers, when it can deliver, and how the product scales. The role is designed for a senior technical leader who is execution-oriented, intellectually honest about risk and remaining work, and energized by the challenge of building a company around genuinely differentiated technology.

About Elessar and Q2 Holodeck™

Elessar is a defense technology company commercializing Q2 Holodeck™, a browser-based, AI/ML-driven, scenario-based training and decision-rehearsal platform. Q2 Holodeck™ helps security, force-protection, and first-responder personnel identify a drone threat, select a lawful and effective response, and coordinate across agencies before a real event occurs. The platform is built to serve defense, homeland security, law enforcement, critical infrastructure, and allied markets.

Our immediate commercial objective is straightforward: release a verified product, land the first paying pilots, and convert those pilots into annual subscriptions and enterprise deployments. The CTO is the person who makes that sequence possible.

What Makes This Opportunity Different

  • Real technology, not a whiteboard. You will lead a platform with working, production-bound code — 75,000+ lines of Go, a live simulation engine, 26 operational scenarios, 93 documented system requirements, and a 24-month roadmap.
  • Direct access and real authority. You will work alongside the CEO, customers, operators, and sales executives — not filtered through layers of product management. You make architecture, security, and delivery decisions.
  • Equity. Your compensation includes possible equity participation in Elessar alongside a competitive base.
  • Founding executive. You will have direct influence over hiring, culture, and strategy as Elessar scales from pilot to enterprise.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Technology Strategy and Architecture (20%). Own the roadmap, translate customer and commercial requirements into engineering priorities, and make and document decisions on platform design, technical debt, integrations, and deployment profiles (cloud, air-gapped, edge).
  • Commercial Release Execution (25%). Lead the 12-week release from funded kickoff to signed pilot acceptance. Establish the delivery baseline, assign accountable owners, manage dependencies, and release against demonstrated security, functional, operational, and customer acceptance criteria. No untested claims ship.
  • Engineering Leadership and Team Building (20%). Recruit, develop, and coordinate software engineering, platform operations, QA, security, and AI/data capabilities. Manage contractors and technology partners. Establish a disciplined software development lifecycle — requirements traceability, code review, automated testing, CI/CD, controlled releases, and clear ownership.
  • Security and Reliability (15%). Own identity and access controls, tenant isolation, secrets management, monitoring, incident response, backup, recovery, and customer-specific assurance requirements. Lead the company toward FedRAMP-compatible and enterprise security posture.
  • AI and Data Engineering (10%). Govern document ingestion, scenario generation, source provenance, retrieval quality, model evaluation, and human review workflows. Preserve the integrity of deterministic simulation behavior and scoring independently of advisory AI layers.
  • Customer and Commercial Support (10%). Participate in technical discovery, demonstrations, proposals, integration planning, and customer assurance reviews. Ensure every commercial commitment reflects tested capabilities and supported configurations. Help Sales close by being the credible technical voice in the room.

Key Performance Objectives

OBJECTIVE - Baseline established

HOW SUCCESS IS MEASURED - Requirements, implemented functionality, outstanding work, staffing, costs, and release-blocking risks reconciled and documented

HORIZON - Month 1

OBJECTIVE - Release candidate delivered

HOW SUCCESS IS MEASURED - Approved instructor and participant workflows, scenario content, scoring, AAR, and operational controls demonstrated on a stable, pinned build

HORIZON - Weeks 8–10

OBJECTIVE - G1 pilot accepted

HOW SUCCESS IS MEASURED - Signed pilot acceptance from a real customer for an explicitly named capacity and configuration; all SRD exceptions visible and dispositioned

HORIZON - Month 3

OBJECTIVE - Team and process in place

HOW SUCCESS IS MEASURED - Release owner named; QA, security, and AI leads identified or contracted; CI/CD and controlled-release discipline operational

HORIZON - Month 3

OBJECTIVE - G2 infrastructure qualified

HOW SUCCESS IS MEASURED - Shared data, tenant isolation, observability, recovery, and increased capacity operational and tested

HORIZON - Month 6

OBJECTIVE - Enterprise posture achieved

HOW SUCCESS IS MEASURED - Enterprise identity, individual learning records, grounded AI assistance, and security certification readiness complete

HORIZON - Month 12

OBJECTIVE - Platform expanded

HOW SUCCESS IS MEASURED - LMS integrations, disconnected/air-gapped deployment, and expanded capacity and content commercially supported

HORIZON - Month 24

Requirements

Qualifications

Required

  • Master’s degree or higher in computer science, engineering, mathematics, data science, or a closely related STEM discipline — or equivalent demonstrated experience at scale.
  • Ten or more years of relevant professional experience in software engineering, architecture, or technical leadership.
  • Prior executive experience at the VP of Engineering, VP of Technology, or CTO level, with accountability for strategy, delivery, staffing, and budgets.
  • Demonstrated success taking software from development or pilot stage into supported commercial operation — including real customers, real security reviews, and real SLAs.
  • Experience leading multidisciplinary teams spanning software engineering, cloud infrastructure, cybersecurity, QA, and AI/data systems.
  • Proven ability to translate business objectives into funded technology roadmaps, measurable delivery commitments, and clear executive reporting.
  • Strong architectural and engineering judgment across cloud applications, real-time systems, APIs, databases, and distributed services.
  • Practical knowledge of application security, DevSecOps, reliability engineering, automated testing, incident management, and AI governance.
  • U.S. citizenship and willingness to complete any customer-required background or security process.

Preferred

  • Experience with simulation, training platforms, or enterprise learning systems.
  • Experience delivering products to government, defense, or public-safety customers — including navigating FedRAMP, ATO processes, or STIG compliance.
  • Familiarity with Go, React/TypeScript, Azure, WebSocket-based real-time systems, LMS interoperability (SCORM/xAPI), and offline or edge deployments.

· Active security clearance.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Execution orientation. Drives toward accepted outcomes — not activity. Knows the difference between code merged and requirement verified.
  • Technical honesty. Reports remaining work, risk, and cost accurately. Never overpromises to leadership or customers to protect a schedule.
  • Commercial instinct. Understands that the product’s purpose is a paying customer, not an elegant architecture. Balances engineering quality with delivery urgency.
  • Team builder. Recruits well, develops people, and creates accountability without bureaucracy.
  • Security judgment. Treats security as a customer requirement, not an afterthought. Knows what a government customer will ask and answers it before they do.
  • Clear communication. Explains technical trade-offs to executives, customers, and engineers without losing precision or patience.
  • Customer partnership. Engages with buyers during the sales cycle, earns technical credibility in discovery, and ensures that what Sales promises is what engineering supports.

Benefits

Compensation and Growth

  • Base salary. Competitive; commensurate with experience and provided during the interview process.
  • Equity. Equity participation in Elessar; structure and terms provided during the interview process.
  • Career growth. The CTO is a founding executive. As Elessar scales from first pilots to enterprise contracts and recurring revenue, the role grows in scope, team size, and market influence. Strong performers will have direct influence over company strategy, hiring, and product direction.

Working Conditions

jobs.title: Chief of Staff (BBS971)
jobs.description:
We're looking for a Chief of Staff to work directly with the CEO of a fast-growing company. You will be the CEO's right hand, owning the operating rhythm, driving cross-functional initiatives, supporting decisions, and protecting the CEO's time, so the CEO can focus on what only the CEO can do.

The goal is leverage, not busyness. As a company grows, the CEO becomes the bottleneck for priorities, follow-through, and decisions. A good chief of staff removes that bottleneck. You will keep the leadership team aligned on what matters, make sure important commitments get done, bring decisions forward with a recommendation instead of a question, and take on special projects that need a trusted owner. You do not need to be the salesperson, the lawyer, or the product manager. You do need strong judgment, a bias for follow-through, and the confidence to tell a CEO "we said this was a priority and it still hasn't happened." The role starts with building core systems and grows into much broader ownership as you learn how the CEO thinks and as the company scales. If you are a systems-minded operator who asks good questions and gets things done, this role is a strong fit.

Why You'll Want to Join

  • You will be paid in USD (bi-monthly: every 15th and 30th)
  • Paid Time Off in accordance with company policy
  • Observance of Holidays per company guidelines
  • 100% remote setup so you can work wherever you're most productive
  • This role requires availability during US business hours
  • Work directly with the CEO of a growing company, with a real seat close to the decisions
  • A role that is built to grow as you do, with a clear plan to hand lower-value work to others as the company scales

What You'll Work On

Operating Rhythm and Priorities

  • Run the company's operating rhythm, including weekly planning, leadership meetings, and regular reviews
  • Track company priorities and goals, and keep the leadership team aligned on what matters most
  • Agree with the CEO on the three outcomes that would make each week successful, and help hold the week to them

Cross-Functional Initiatives and Follow-Through

  • Drive important initiatives across teams, making sure each has a clear owner, timeline, next action, and known blockers
  • Track commitments and follow-ups from meetings and from partners, vendors, customers, and team members, and make sure they get done
  • Flag what is overdue, what has stalled, and what needs the CEO to move forward

Decision Support and Special Projects

  • Bring decisions to the CEO with the situation, the realistic options, your recommendation, and the decision needed
  • Run a decision queue so the CEO can clear accumulated decisions in a short session instead of being interrupted all day
  • Own research, analysis, and special projects that need a trusted, capable owner
  • Prepare briefings, updates, and materials for leadership and key stakeholders

CEO Time and Communications

  • Help design how the CEO's time is used by asking whether the CEO needs to be in a meeting, whether someone else could handle it, or whether it can be resolved asynchronously
  • Protect time for planning, strategy, and key relationships, and treat it like real meetings
  • Triage the CEO's inbox and surface only what needs the CEO's response or decision
  • Prepare the CEO for important meetings with context and goals, and follow up with decisions, commitments, and next actions

Learning the CEO and the Business

  • Learn the CEO's preferences and decision patterns, and build a living operating playbook covering scheduling, communication, priorities, approvals, and what to escalate
  • Ask whether each piece of direction is a one-time exception or a standing rule, and record the answer
  • Learn the company's offering, customers, and strategy well enough to represent it accurately and recognize what matters
  • Regularly ask what the CEO is doing that someone else could do, and propose processes that remove that work

Requirements

What You Bring

  • Experience as a chief of staff, senior operator, or strategy and operations lead supporting a founder or CEO, with a record of building systems and not only completing tasks
  • Strong judgment about what needs the CEO and what you can handle, and the confidence to push back when priorities slip
  • Proven follow-through across many people and teams, chasing commitments without being asked
  • Project management skills and the ability to drive work across functions without formal authority
  • Analytical ability and clear, concise writing that turns messy information into a short, useful update
  • Curiosity and willingness to ask questions, including ones you feel you should already know the answer to
  • Discretion with confidential and commercial information
  • Comfort using AI tools and tracking and collaboration tools to work faster
  • Excellent written and spoken English
  • Available to work full-time during US business hours

Nice to Have

  • Experience supporting a founder or CEO at a small, fast-growing company
  • Background in operations, strategy, consulting, or program management
  • Experience building operating playbooks, trackers, and decision processes
  • Experience running leadership meetings, goal-setting cycles, or company planning

How to Apply

Please include:

  1. Your updated resume
  2. A short Loom video (1 to 2 minutes) introducing yourself, describing your chief of staff or senior operations experience, and walking through a system or process you built to keep a leader's priorities and commitments on track

Only candidates who submit a Loom video will be moved to the next step of the hiring process.

If you want to build the systems and judgment that let a CEO focus on what only they can do, and you want a role that grows as you prove yourself, this role gives you the access and the direct impact to do your best work.

Benefits

Application Process Overview

Our comprehensive selection process ensures we find the right fit for both you and our clients:

  1. Initial Application - Submit your application and complete our prequalifying questions
  2. Video Introduction - Record a video introduction to showcase your communication skills and work experience
  3. Role-Specific Assessment - Complete a homework assignment tailored to the position (if applicable)
  4. Recruitment Interview - Initial screening with our talent team
  5. Executive Interview - Meet with senior leadership to discuss role alignment
  6. Client Interview - Final interview with the client team you'd be supporting
  7. Background & Reference Check - Professional reference verification
  8. Job Offer - Successful candidates receive a formal offer to join the team

Each stage is designed to evaluate your fit for the role while giving you insights into our company culture and expectations. We'll keep you informed throughout the process and provide feedback at each step.

Are you ready to make a difference in the world and become part of our patient-centered team that is focused on Attacking Bladder Cancer for a Better Tomorrow? Every day we are making significant advancements across our multiple pipelines and are growing rapidly to meet the needs of our patients who cannot afford to wait to benefit from our novel immunotherapies. Please review this job posting and our Values and if they resonate with you and are what you expect from your organization and team, then we would like to hear from you.

About the role

The Associate Director, Procurement will support the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of CG Oncology’s procurement operations, purchasing policies, and procure-to-pay (P2P) processes. Reporting to the VP, Controller, this hands-on role will partner cross-functionally with Finance, Legal, IT, Quality, and business stakeholders to strengthen procurement controls, streamline vendor management, and improve operational efficiency. The Associate Director will play a key role in procurement technology implementation and optimization, supplier negotiations, and the development of scalable processes that enhance spend visibility, compliance, and organizational effectiveness. This role will combine functional expertise with hands-on execution to support CG Oncology’s evolving business needs.

Essential Functions

  • Define functional requirements and process flows to inform CLM platform selection and implementation planning.
  • Serve as functional owner for Coupa and CLM post-implementation, including enhancements, UAT, workflow controls, reporting, and automation
  • Maintain the P2P/CLM RACI across business owners, Legal, FP&A, Accounting, Procurement, and IT.
  • Own the contract-to-PO process, aligning negotiated contract terms with PO issuance and financial approvals.
  • Maintain all vendor records, approvals, POs and associated documentation in accordance with SOX 404(b) standards
  • Partner with department owners to write RFPs and BRDs for new project or vendors as needed
  • Monitor contract renewals, expirations, and change orders to support continuity of supply.
  • Partner with Quality, IT, and Accounting to standardize vendor onboarding, qualification, and system access.
  • Meet regularly with Accounts Payable to resolve aging invoices, unapproved proxies, and PO/invoice mismatches.
  • Resolve rejected vendor records, W-9 corrections, and vendor master data issues.
  • Establish supplier performance management, including service levels, pricing compliance, recurring issues, and supplier escalations.
  • Coordinate with Accounting/AP, FP&A, and business owners to resolve PO overages and payment exceptions.
  • Assist Accounting team with month-end close by gathering accrual information for open POs
  • Establish and enforce approval matrices, delegation-of-authority thresholds, and segregation-of-duties controls in partnership with Finance.
  • Develop and implement Purchasing Policy and SOPs covering PO creation, strategic sourcing, and vendor onboarding.
  • Create training resources and deliver organization-wide purchasing policy education. Conduct periodical refresher training sessions as needed to improve end user efficiency.
  • Optimize P2P workflows from sourcing and intake through contracts, onboarding, approvals, receiving, invoicing, and payment.
  • Serve as the central contact for PO and invoice exception troubleshooting.
  • Maintain a savings tracker to identify and report cost savings, rebates, and volume discounts.
  • Lead supplier negotiations, including pricing, payment terms, rate cards, discounts, renewals, and other commercial terms, in partnership with Legal and business owners.
  • Develop and report P2P KPIs (retrospective POs, blocked invoices, first-pass match, onboarding cycle time, missed discounts, and recurring exceptions), and lead root-cause reviews that drive corrective actions to closure.
  • Maintain current supplier records in the system to enable sending documents to the vendors directly from the system

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Supply Chain Management, Finance, Accounting, or related field; equivalent relevant experience may be considered
  • 8+ years of progressive experience in procurement, purchasing, procure-to-pay operations, or related finance operations
  • Hands-on experience with purchase orders, vendor onboarding, invoice exceptions, and cross-functional process coordination
  • Working knowledge of purchasing policies, approval workflows, internal controls, and vendor master data
  • Ability to develop SOPs, train stakeholders, and manage multiple priorities independently
  • Strong written communication, analytical, and problem-solving skills
  • Ability to operate as both strategic functional lead and hands-on problem solver in an evolving organization
  • Highly detail-oriented and consistent in reviewing PO line items (descriptions, project, quantities, pricing, service periods, and GL/project coding) for accuracy, contract alignment, and audit readiness
  • Demonstrated experience configuring or administering Coupa workflows, approval chains, and reporting

jobs.title: Online Data Analyst - Spanish speakers (MX)
jobs.description:
About the Role

Millions of people rely on digital maps every day to navigate, to discover, to find their way. But maps are only as accurate as the data behind them, and data is only as trustworthy as the people who verify it. Your knowledge of Mexico's geography, local landmarks, and how people actually navigate your region is something no algorithm can fully replicate. That local intelligence is what makes maps genuinely useful.

Why This Matters

Accurately verified mapping data prevents real-world navigation errors. Your verification work ensures that:

  • Users can discover trusted businesses and cultural landmarks with confidence

  • Communities can navigate with accurate, culturally-informed geographic intelligence

  • Geographic data quality scales across millions of locations and thousands of data variations

At scale, this is infrastructure work. Every verified data point contributes to how billions of people interact with geographic information globally.

What You'll Do

Core Responsibilities

Structured Quality Audits on Spatial Datasets

  • Conduct detailed, methodical evaluations of geographic and business data entries using advanced mapping platforms and GIS-standard evaluation tools

  • Assess spatial data points (coordinates, boundaries, locations) for accuracy and consistency across multiple authoritative sources

  • Verify business information (names, hours, categories, contact details, service offerings) against primary and secondary sources

  • Evaluate cultural and regional context—ensuring data reflects how Mexicans actually navigate, describe, and interact with their geographic environment

Cross-Reference Complex Data Against Authoritative Sources

  • Compare business, geographic, and cultural data entries across multiple authoritative sources (official registries, local government databases, business directories, street-level verification)

  • Identify discrepancies where data conflicts across sources (e.g., conflicting addresses, outdated hours, category misclassifications)

  • Apply critical thinking to determine which source is most reliable and document reasoning transparently

Rigorous Framework Application

  • Apply detailed, multi-dimensional evaluation frameworks with consistency and precision across dozens of geographic, business, and cultural data variations

  • Understand the intent behind evaluation guidelines and apply them contextually—knowing when to follow rules strictly and when to apply judgment

Work Across Diverse Task Types

  • Be flexible and adaptable across varied evaluation tasks: Maps (location data, boundaries), News (geo-relevant content accuracy), Audio (transcription and context verification), Relevance (data-to-query matching), and emerging task types

  • Quickly learn new task specifications and apply them with the same rigor

Provide Structured Feedback for Algorithm Improvement

  • Articulate clear, actionable feedback that helps refine mapping algorithms and improve geographic intelligence

  • Explain not just what is wrong, but why it matters for real-world navigation and discovery

  • Suggest data corrections that are specific, evidence-based, and prioritize the most impactful improvements

Why join the project:

  • Structured onboarding: Access comprehensive evaluation guidelines, detailed reference materials, and practical examples before your first live assessment

  • Direct feedback and growth: Receive performance assessments tied to quality metrics so you can refine your evaluation precision

  • Intellectually rigorous work: Each evaluation requires methodical reasoning, framework interpretation, and structured discrepancy analysis.

Mandatory Qualifications

Language Proficiency

  • Professional fluency in both English and Spanish (native or near-native proficiency required in both languages)

  • Must be able to read and write formal evaluations clearly and precisely in English

  • Must understand Spanish-language geographic, business, and cultural context

  • Must be comfortable with technical terminology in both languages

Geographic and Residency Requirements

  • Current residency in Mexico for the last 5 consecutive years (required to ensure authentic, current geographic knowledge)

  • Deep, lived knowledge of Mexico's geography—including major cities, regional landmarks, state and municipal boundaries, and less-prominent areas

  • Current understanding of how people in your region actually navigate, speak about locations, and describe directions (colloquial usage, cultural references, regional variations)

Analytical and Problem-Solving Capability

  • Advanced analytical thinking: demonstrated ability to break down complex geographic and business information into component parts, analyze each critically, and synthesize findings

  • Methodical problem-solving: comfort with systematic approaches to identifying and resolving data discrepancies; ability to think through multiple hypotheses

  • Attention to detail: capacity to spot inconsistencies, errors, and anomalies across large datasets without losing focus

Evaluation Framework Mastery

  • Comfort with rigorous guideline interpretation: ability to understand detailed evaluation frameworks, ask clarifying questions, and apply them consistently across diverse scenarios

  • Consistency under complexity: capacity to maintain consistent standards while handling dozens of variations in geographic, business, and cultural data

  • Documentation discipline: willingness to articulate reasoning clearly in writing, so that your decisions can be audited and learned from

Task Flexibility

  • Openness to working across diverse task types (Maps, News, Audio, Relevance, and emerging domains)

  • Ability to learn new task specifications quickly and apply them with the same rigor as established tasks

  • Adaptability to shifting priorities and project needs

Technical Literacy

  • Comfortable learning and using mapping platforms and data evaluation interfaces

  • Able to navigate web-based tools, upload files, and troubleshoot basic technical issues

  • No programming experience required; willingness to learn new tools is essential

﻿

Technical Requirements

  • Stable, reliable internet connection (minimum 5 Mbps download/upload recommended)

  • Personal computer or laptop with current operating system, functioning keyboard, and mouse

  • Quiet, distraction-free workspace for focused evaluation work

Qualification path

Assessment

In order to be hired into the program, you’ll take an open book qualification exam that will determine your suitability for the position and complete ID verification. jobs.title: Field Clinical Specialist
jobs.description:
ABOUT ORGANOX:

OrganOx is a commercial stage organ technology company dedicated to developing technologies to improve outcomes for patients with acute or chronic organ failure. The company was established as a spin out of the University of Oxford in 2008 and is now part of the Terumo Group. OrganOx is a pioneer in normothermic machine perfusion (NMP). It's flagship platform, the metra®, is available for use in the U.S., Europe, Canada, and Australia. It has been utilized in over 7,000 liver transplants to date to keep donor livers in a metabolically active state outside the body enabling longer preservation times and functional assessment of the organ prior to transplant, leading to an increased number of organs available for transplant. Founded in 1921, Terumo Corporation (TSE:4543) strives to fulfil its mission of “Contributing to Society through Healthcare” by providing a comprehensive range of solutions in the fields of therapeutic procedures, hospital operations, and life sciences in more than 160 countries and regions.

Position Summary

The Field Clinical Specialist will be responsible for the training, support and adoption of OrganOx’s products. This includes teaching and training users in the correct manner to ensure our products are used safely and effectively - for the preservation of organs prior to transplant.

They are the first point of contact for the customer and maintain the relationship with the relevant clinical transplant teams. The role is home based but will require frequent travel to allocated transplantation centres (40%-60%) for on-site training, support or review meetings. They will partake in the 24/7 on-call rota (including weekends and holidays) for on-site or remote support.

The Field Clinical Specialist will be responsible for promoting the benefits of OrganOx’s products with customers, facilitating the sharing of customer experiences to support adoption of OrganOx products and for arranging user groups to facilitate shared learning. The Field Clinical Specialist should develop an in-depth knowledge of machine perfusion and published articles, including NMP, HMP and NRP to facilitate this.

The Field Clinical Specialist will track the account performance, clinical progression, supports forecasting of system usage and consumables set allocation. They ensure customer data are maintained in the relevant database and all regulatory customer consent is collected and documented. They will support the Commercial management team in prospecting and generating new customer leads and actively support commercial projects.

The Field Clinical Specialist will work with all relevant functional teams in OrganOx. They ensure all service-related problems are resolved according to customer and contractual expectations. They will own and support customer complaint and feedback recording and provide information to the OrganOx Quality and Regulatory team. They will report product related feedback to the relevant design and engineering colleagues.

This is a remote position in the UK with regular travel across Europe.

Listed below are the major responsibilities of the role and a brief description of some of the key tasks to be performed. This list is not totally exhaustive.

Major Responsibilities

Under direction from the VP Commercial, Europe the Field Clinical Specialist will be responsible for:

Training and Support

  • Train and support transplant teams in the use of the OrganOx metra. Ensure that all users understand the operation modes on the device (with and without an organ in place).
  • Ensure that all centres and teams remain competent in the use of the device by a process of in-person follow-up on a regular basis. Ensure that existing and new team members are trained and certified.
  • Contribute towards a 24-hour, 7 days a week on-call technical support rota, ensuring that there is always a Clinical Specialist available to deal and resolve enquiries.
  • Ensure that all calls are logged, and any outstanding issues are followed up and resolved. Collect all information and disseminate to team members and other users as appropriate.

Adoption of OrganOx Products

  • Establish and maintain customer relationships, sharing best practice to support adoption of the metra. Develop adoption strategies and materials to showcase the benefits of the metra. Present these materials and strategies to customers.
  • Identify and develop "champions" of the technology at each customer site.
  • Identify relevant customer contacts, record and maintain customer database in accordance with data protection regulations.
  • Identify potential new users of OrganOx products and work with the commercial management on preparing the supply offer. Document market leads and projects in the relevant database and track the progress accurately
  • Work with transplant teams to collect data on organs perfused and preserved on the metra to build up a database of product performance and use.
  • Help to collect information about organ transplantation in general, the preferences and needs of individual units and the status of competing technologies.
  • Maintain the database of procedures carried out per centre, the types of organs transplanted and the cases where the metra has been used.
  • Support user group meetings to facilitate shared learning and best practice.

Support for Research and Development, Quality and Sales & Marketing Functions

  • Report any issues or feedback reported with the metra to the Quality team, ensuring prompt completion of follow-up actions.
  • Assist marketing personnel in understanding the marketplace, utilising knowledge of customers, hospitals, working practices etc.
  • Maintain accurate records of all training procedures.
  • Evaluate the quality of training delivered as an ongoing and cumulative process.
  • Provide a report on the status of each centre with respect to the installation and training procedures.

Additional Responsibilities

  • Maintaining good laboratory practice, adhering to SOPs and ensuring excellent record keeping. Treat animal and human tissue with due care and in accordance with SOPs and policies.
  • Continued professional development, for example studying medical journals to ensure your knowledge of the transplantation and medical device field is current.
  • Adhere to the letter and spirit of OrganOx’s Code of Conduct and all other company policies

Requirements

Skills & Experience

  • Demonstrable experience in a clinical or healthcare science environment (essential)
  • Experience in training users of medical devices (essential)
  • Able to provide support during surgical procedures (essential)
  • Broad knowledge and experience of working in operating theatres, recovery units and intensive care units (essential)
  • Excellent interpersonal and presentation skills, and the ability to work with customers of varying background and abilities (essential)
  • Ability to understand scientific publications in detail to develop an in-depth knowledge of machine perfusion, including competing technologies (HMP, NRP) (essential)
  • Friendly, approachable and customer focused approach to work (essential)
  • Be able to travel regularly within the UK and Europe, and elsewhere as required (essential)
  • Analytical approach to problem solving (essential)
  • Good technical, manual and dexterity skills (essential)
  • Ability to work alone (essential)
  • Willing to work long and unpredictable hours (essential)
  • Experience working in a laboratory (desirable)
  • Conversant in medical terminology and an understanding of systems and processes within the human body (desirable)
  • Up to date with new techniques and developments for the promotion and maintenance of good practice (desirable)
  • Prepared to accept a high degree of responsibility (desirable)
  • Highly observant of people and procedures (desirable)

jobs.title: Purchasing Planning Manager
jobs.description:
Position Summary:

The Planning Manager is a leadership role responsible for the overall strategy, direction, and execution of the inventory planning function across all stocked product categories, including Wallcovering, Fabric, Furnishings, and carpet. This role is accountable for leading the team, developing world-class demand forecasts, optimizing inventory investment and ensuring product availability to support sales growth and maximize working capital efficiency. The Manager drives continuous improvement in planning processes and tools, manages key vendor relationships strategically, and serves as the primary liaison between Planning and senior leadership from Procurement, Category Management Team (CMT), Sales, and Operations. Expect high-level strategic thinking, decisive team leadership, and ultimate accountability for overall inventory health.

Key Responsibilities:

Team Leadership & Development

  • Lead, mentor, and develop a team of Inventory Planners and Senior Planners.

  • Set team strategy, goals, and priorities, and monitor progress toward overall inventory objectives.

  • Oversee performance management, coaching, and training of team members, fostering a culture of high performance and accuracy.

  • Responsible for distributing information to the team from upper management.

Inventory Strategy & Demand Planning

  • Responsible for setting and maintaining the overall inventory investment strategy across all assigned product categories.

  • Direct the development of robust, rolling demand forecasts using advanced historical sales data (30/60/90-day trends), seasonal patterns, and project pipeline inputs.

  • Establish, audit, and maintain core inventory parameters (reorder points, safety stock) across the team to minimize risk and optimize working capital.

  • Proactively monitor and manage inventory health metrics, including aged inventory exposure, stockout risks, and overstock situations.

Supply Chain & Vendor Management

  • Oversee the strategic partnership with key wallcovering, fabric, and furnishing vendors to secure supply and negotiate optimal production schedules and order quantities.

  • Lead the coordination with Purchasing teams to determine buy quantities, replenishment timing, and mitigate high-risk supply disruptions.

  • Directly manage the review of supplier performance for delivery and service level, implementing necessary improvement plans.

  • Manage inventory exposure across key mills and suppliers.

Reporting, Analysis & Process Improvement

  • Design, develop, and maintain advanced inventory performance dashboards and weekly health reports for senior leadership.

  • Oversee the monitoring of forecast accuracy and bias across the team, implementing corrective actions to forecasting models and planning tools.

  • Identify, champion, and implement strategic improvements to planning tools, processes, and reporting capabilities across the organization.

Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Serve as the primary inventory planning partner to the Category Management Team (CMT) to align buying strategies and uphold product & vendor goals.

  • Partner with sales teams to incorporate customer demand insights and upcoming project requirements.

  • Collaborate with warehouse and operations teams to manage stock allocation and replenishment, including coordinating transport of goods.

  • And other duties as assigned.

Requirements

Abilities/Key Competencies/Skills:

  • Proven experience leading and mentoring a team in a complex planning or supply chain environment.

  • Expert-level demand forecasting and inventory planning experience with experience analyzing large SKU assortments.

  • Advanced proficiency in ERP/inventory systems (e.g., Oracle) and data analysis tools (Advanced Excel/Google Sheets data analysis skills with Pivot tables, Forecast modeling, Data visualization) required.

  • Exceptional strategic thinking, critical problem-solving skills, and the ability to contribute innovative ideas.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to present complex data and strategy clearly to executive leadership and focus on a high customer service level.

  • Deep understanding of core inventory metrics (Weeks of Supply, Sell-through, Safety stock, Forecast accuracy).

  • Detail-oriented & High level of accuracy.

  • Curiosity and willingness to learn and grow within the organization.

  • Knowledge and experience with using Asana as a project management tool (Preferred).

Fabric, Wallcovering and Furnishing Planning Knowledge (Preferred):

  • Maintain a comprehensive working knowledge of wallcovering, fabric, and furnishing constructions, mill production processes, and supply chains in order to effectively manage inventory planning for assigned product categories as well as provide informed guidance to cross-functional partners.

  • Expertise in fabric and wallcovering yardage planning and managing product colorways/SKUs.

  • Deep awareness of vendor production lead times and knowledge of inventory challenges in stocked wallcovering, fabric, and furnishings.

  • Possess expert knowledge of mill MOQ’s and price break structures, leveraging this insight to optimize order quantities and support high-level cost negotiations with vendors when appropriate.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs):

The Planning Manager is accountable for the overall performance of the Inventory Planning team, optimizing the company's inventory investment, and maximizing product availability.

  • Overall Forecast Accuracy & Bias: Measures the aggregate effectiveness of the team's demand forecasting.

  • Inventory Investment Efficiency: Tracks inventory dollars relative to revenue and working capital goals.

  • Aged Inventory Reduction: Measures strategic management and minimization of slow-moving or obsolete inventory.

  • In-Stock Rate & Stockout Rate: Measures overall product availability and service level performance across core categories.

  • Weeks of Supply Optimization: Measures success in maintaining inventory within targeted strategic levels.

  • Team Development & Process Leadership: Measures effectiveness in mentoring planners, strengthening planning capabilities, and maintaining consistent planning processes across the team.

Experience/Certifications/Education:

  • Minimum 7+ years’ progressive experience in Inventory Planning, Demand Planning, or Supply Chain, with at least 3 years in a leadership or managerial role required.

  • Home decor or textile industry knowledge is preferred.

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, or a related field required; Master’s Degree or Supply Chain Certification (e.g., APICS) preferred (Elevated from Bachelor’s Degree preferred).

  • This is a fully remote role, though candidates residing on Long Island are preferred for occasional in-person team meetings or collaboration.

  • Salary Range: $85,000 - $95,000

jobs.description:
Recruiter (Talent Acquisition, LinkedIn Recruiter & ATS) – Remote

Talent Acquisition | LinkedIn Recruiter | Full-Cycle Recruitment | U.S. Hiring

Position Type: Full-Time, Remote
Working Hours: U.S. Client Business Hours (flexibility required for interviews and candidate availability)

About the Role

At Pavago, one of our clients is hiring a Recruiter to manage the full recruitment lifecycle—from sourcing and screening to offer management and onboarding coordination.

This is a hands-on talent acquisition role where you’ll build strong candidate pipelines, engage top talent, partner with hiring managers, and drive efficient hiring processes across multiple industries and business functions.

You’ll play a key role in ensuring hiring moves quickly without compromising quality, while delivering an exceptional experience for both candidates and hiring managers.

If you thrive in fast-paced recruitment environments and understand that successful hiring requires strong sourcing, communication, organization, and sound judgment, this role is an excellent fit.

What You’ll Own

Hiring Strategy & Role Planning

  • Partner with hiring managers to understand hiring needs, ideal candidate profiles, and recruitment priorities.
  • Develop sourcing strategies based on market conditions and hiring urgency.
  • Write clear, SEO-optimized job descriptions that attract qualified candidates.
  • Advise stakeholders on hiring timelines, market trends, and talent availability.

Candidate Sourcing & Pipeline Development

  • Build qualified talent pipelines using LinkedIn Recruiter, Indeed, Glassdoor, and other job boards.
  • Source passive candidates using Boolean search techniques and outbound outreach.
  • Maintain active candidate pipelines across multiple open positions.
  • Continuously improve sourcing strategies and response rates.

Candidate Screening & Assessment

  • Conduct structured phone and video interviews.
  • Evaluate candidates based on technical skills, communication, experience, and cultural fit.
  • Utilize behavioral interviewing and competency-based assessment techniques.
  • Coordinate assessments, case studies, or technical evaluations when required.

Candidate Experience

  • Manage candidate communication from initial outreach through offer acceptance.
  • Ensure timely responses, clear expectations, and consistent follow-up.
  • Represent both the client and employer brand professionally throughout the hiring process.
  • Deliver a positive, transparent, and engaging candidate experience.

Interview Coordination & Hiring Support

  • Coordinate interviews across multiple time zones.
  • Prepare candidates for interview stages.
  • Gather structured interview feedback from hiring teams.
  • Facilitate hiring discussions and support decision-making.

Offer Management & Onboarding

  • Prepare and present employment offers.
  • Support offer negotiations professionally.
  • Coordinate pre-onboarding activities and smooth candidate transitions.
  • Maintain communication through the onboarding process.

Recruitment Operations & Reporting

  • Manage hiring workflows within ATS platforms such as Greenhouse, Lever, JazzHR, iCIMS, or similar systems.
  • Track recruiting metrics including time-to-fill, pipeline health, source effectiveness, and candidate progression.
  • Maintain accurate recruitment dashboards and reports.
  • Share hiring insights and market feedback with leadership.

Requirements

Must-Have Qualifications

Experience

  • 2+ years of experience in Talent Acquisition, Recruiting, or Staffing.
  • Experience managing full-cycle recruitment processes.
  • Experience recruiting across multiple functions or industries.

Technical Skills

  • Strong experience using LinkedIn Recruiter and major job boards.
  • Proficiency with Boolean search techniques and outbound sourcing.
  • Hands-on experience using Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS).
  • Strong interviewing and candidate evaluation skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal English communication skills.
  • Ability to work remotely during U.S. business hours.

Nice-to-Have

  • Agency or high-volume recruiting experience.
  • Experience hiring for SaaS, Finance, Professional Services, Property Management, or Operations roles.
  • Knowledge of employment laws, hiring compliance, and recruitment analytics.
  • Experience mentoring recruiters or improving recruiting processes.

Tools & Platforms

  • LinkedIn Recruiter
  • Indeed
  • Glassdoor
  • Greenhouse
  • Lever
  • JazzHR
  • iCIMS
  • Google Workspace
  • Microsoft Office

What Makes You a Strong Fit

  • Strategic thinker with a hands-on execution mindset.
  • Strong sourcing and relationship-building skills.
  • Excellent organizational and multitasking abilities.
  • Comfortable managing multiple requisitions simultaneously.
  • Strong communicator with candidates, hiring managers, and leadership.
  • Ownership-driven and focused on delivering quality hiring outcomes.

What a Typical Day Looks Like

  • Source candidates through LinkedIn Recruiter and job boards.
  • Review applications and conduct candidate screenings.
  • Coordinate interviews with hiring managers.
  • Update ATS records and recruitment pipelines.
  • Follow up with candidates throughout the hiring process.
  • Share market insights and hiring updates with stakeholders.
  • Track recruiting metrics and prioritize open requisitions.

In short: You build high-quality talent pipelines, guide candidates through an exceptional hiring experience, and help organizations make great hiring decisions efficiently.

Key Metrics for Success (KPIs)

  • Time-to-fill within target benchmarks
  • Candidate quality and interview-to-hire conversion rate
  • Hiring manager satisfaction
  • Candidate experience and communication quality
  • ATS accuracy and reporting consistency
  • Pipeline health and sourcing effectiveness

Why This Role Stands Out

  • Fully remote opportunity supporting U.S.-based hiring.
  • Full ownership of the end-to-end recruitment lifecycle.
  • Exposure to multiple industries and business functions.
  • Direct impact on company growth through strategic hiring.
  • Career growth into Senior Recruiter, Talent Acquisition Lead, or Recruiting Manager roles.

Interview Process

  1. Initial Phone Screen
  2. Spark Hire Intro Video (3–5 minutes)
  3. Practical Assessment (Boolean Search & Candidate Sourcing Exercise)
  4. Client Interview
  5. Offer & Background Verification

What Happens After You Apply

Right after you apply, you’ll receive an email invitation from Spark Hire to record your Intro Video. This short, self-recorded video is the next step that completes your application and can be recorded whenever it’s convenient for you.

Instead of repeating yourself across multiple screening calls, you’ll introduce yourself once, and your video will be shared with the hiring team. This helps the hiring team evaluate your communication style early, making future interviews more meaningful while reducing unnecessary interview rounds.

Don’t overthink it—you can record your video as many times as you’d like before submitting it. Only your final submission will be reviewed.

Please keep an eye on both your inbox and spam folder for your Spark Hire invitation after submitting your application.

Apply Now

If you’re a driven Recruiter who enjoys sourcing exceptional talent, managing full-cycle hiring, and delivering an outstanding candidate experience, we’d love to hear from you. Apply today and help build high-performing teams for growing organizations.

jobs.title: Business Development Attorney — Personal Injury Case Acquisition
jobs.description:
About CasesDaily

We are a software-driven case-acquisition platform for plaintiff personal injury firms. We sell exclusive, AI-qualified car accident leads, priced per qualified lead, on top of an AI CRM and follow-up system most of the field does not have. The company was built by people who signed hundreds of PI cases and ran intake, so we sell to firm owners as peers. We work with more than a dozen firms today.

What makes the product different

  • Case quality, not volume. One case is worth $5,000 to a firm. Another is worth $100,000. We know the difference and we screen for it, so firms get cases worth signing.
  • AI qualifying and follow-up. Our software qualifies and warms every lead before a firm ever sees it, then keeps working it with automated follow-up.
  • Compliance built into the tech. Consent capture and compliance live inside the platform, not bolted on after, (including California SB37 compliance) which is what keeps the firms we sell to safe.

The opportunity

Selling qualified case leads is a small, quiet field. Fewer than a hundred companies do it seriously, and almost none bring real attorney and intake experience the way we do.

This is not a high-volume sales job. A single firm can order around $100,000 a month. A dozen strong relationships can add over $1.5 million a month in billing. You build and keep a short list of high-value firm relationships, with uncapped commission on every one. Two dozen good clients is a career.

Why an attorney

Firm owners buy from people they trust and who speak their language. Your license puts you in the room as a peer, not a vendor, and you understand the compliance that keeps those firms safe, which becomes one of your strongest selling points.

In today’s marketing, making equity partner at a firm turns on business development more than billable work, and the equity tier keeps shrinking. This role builds that exact skill right now, with full support from a team, and no waiting ten years for a committee to maybe review.

What you'd do

  • Run discovery calls with firm owners: cost per lead, close rate, cost per signed case, and the volume they can handle.
  • Turn that into a proof order and a path to locking up their market, then close it.
  • Manage the firms you sign so they keep buying and grow their orders.
  • Carry compliance as a value-add: TCPA and consent, DNC and reassigned numbers, California SB37, CAN-SPAM, A2P 10DLC, and Google Ads policy.

Who you are

  • A licensed attorney in good standing.
  • You build trust fast and can sign another attorney without it feeling like a pitch.
  • Personal injury experience and firm relationships are a plus.
  • Comfortable in an early company where some of what you need does not exist yet.

Compensation

  • An hourly rate for your legal and compliance work, so your expertise is paid from day one.
  • Uncapped commission on every firm you sign and manage.
  • A defined path to ownership for the person who proves the fit. That is a conversation, not a number in a job ad.

Logistics

Remote, hours you control. You work directly with the founders as the first attorney in the company.

How to apply

Skip the cover letter. Tell us about a deal or a case you closed and what it took to get it done. If you have personal injury relationships, tell us about those too.

jobs.title: Financial Analyst - FP&A
jobs.description:
Financial Analyst – FP&A

Position Type: Full-Time, Remote

Working Hours: U.S. Business Hours

About the Role

We are looking for a detail-oriented and analytical Financial Analyst – FP&A to help leadership make smarter financial decisions through accurate reporting, forecasting, and business analysis.

In this role, you will work closely with the CEO, Accounting Manager, and external consultants to analyze company performance, build financial reports, monitor profitability, and support strategic planning across multiple business locations.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys working with numbers, identifying business trends, and turning financial data into meaningful insights.

Responsibilities

Financial Analysis & Reporting

  • Build and maintain financial models for revenue, expenses, margins, and EBITDA.
  • Prepare weekly and monthly financial reports for leadership.
  • Analyze business performance across multiple locations and identify trends.
  • Monitor profitability and recommend opportunities to improve financial performance.

Forecasting & Planning

  • Support the company's 13-week cash flow forecast.
  • Update financial forecasts and identify potential financial risks.
  • Assist with budgeting and long-term financial planning.

Business Insights

  • Analyze financial and CRM data to identify revenue trends, cost variances, and profit opportunities.
  • Present findings and recommendations in a clear and easy-to-understand manner.
  • Prepare reports and presentations for leadership meetings.

Collaboration

  • Work closely with the CEO, Accounting Manager, and external consultants on financial planning and company strategy.
  • Support projects that help the company prepare for future growth.

What Makes You a Strong Fit

  • You enjoy analyzing financial data and solving business problems.
  • You can explain financial information in a simple and practical way.
  • You pay close attention to detail and enjoy working with numbers.
  • You are proactive and comfortable working independently.

Required Experience & Skills

Must-Have

  • 2–3 years of experience in Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A), Financial Analysis, or Accounting.
  • Strong understanding of accounting principles and financial statements.
  • Experience preparing financial reports, forecasts, and business analysis.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel.
  • Experience using QuickBooks Online.
  • Experience with Power BI, Tableau, or similar reporting tools.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal English communication skills.

Nice-to-Have

  • Experience supporting multi-location or multi-entity businesses.
  • Experience with budgeting and cash flow forecasting.
  • Familiarity with CRM reporting and business performance analysis.
  • CPA or other accounting/finance certification is a plus.

What Does a Typical Day Look Like?

Your day starts by reviewing financial reports and updating key business metrics. You analyze revenue, expenses, profitability, and cash flow, then prepare reports that help leadership understand how the business is performing.

Throughout the day, you update financial models, identify trends, investigate unusual financial results, and work with the CEO and Accounting Manager on planning and strategic projects.

Success in this role comes from providing accurate financial insights that help the company make better business decisions.
