jobs.title: Healthcare Operations Coordinator (BBS962)
jobs.description:
We're looking for a Healthcare Operations Coordinator to support both patient and clinician administrative operations at an early-stage, venture-backed virtual pediatric specialty care practice focused on weight and metabolic health. You will help families register, schedule, and stay on track with their care, and help the clinician team stay organized, credentialed, and supported as the practice launches across multiple US states.

This is not a purely executive assistant role. It sits inside a healthcare operations environment, so you will coordinate several workflows at once, communicate professionally with patients and clinicians, and keep accurate records. You will work closely with the Head of Operations and a planned Care Operations Lead. The practice is small and processes are still being built, so you will have real ownership and a hand in shaping how things run. If you have supported a US-based healthcare organization, know your way around an EHR, and have good judgment about when to resolve something yourself and when to escalate, this role is a strong fit.

Why You'll Want to Join

  • Get paid in USD (bi-monthly: every 15th and 30th)
  • Paid Time Off in accordance with company policy
  • Observance of Holidays per company guidelines
  • 100% remote setup so you can work wherever you're most productive (requires availability during US business hours)
  • Join at launch and help build a care model from the ground up
  • Work directly with the operations leadership of a small, mission-driven team

What You'll Work On

Patient Operations and Support

  • Triage and respond to routine patient and family inquiries through approved phone, email, text, and portal channels
  • Route messages to clinicians for response as needed and make sure every patient gets an answer
  • Assist families with registration, onboarding, and appointment scheduling
  • Follow up on incomplete intake forms, consents, and required documentation
  • Coordinate appointment confirmations, reminders, cancellations, and rescheduling
  • Help families navigate the administrative side of their care
  • Track outstanding patient requests until resolved
  • Escalate complex questions, complaints, and clinical concerns to the right team member

Clinician Operations and Administrative Support

  • Maintain accurate clinician rosters, availability, scheduling records, and administrative files
  • Track state licenses, expiration dates, and renewal deadlines
  • Follow up with clinicians to collect required documents and information
  • Assist with onboarding checklists and administrative setup for new clinicians
  • Update credentialing and payer enrollment trackers
  • Coordinate routine follow-ups with clinicians, credentialing partners, and other vendors
  • Support recruiting coordination, including interview scheduling and candidate follow-ups

General Operations Support

  • Maintain operational trackers, spreadsheets, and shared documentation
  • Monitor shared inboxes and route requests to the right owners
  • Follow up on outstanding tasks and deadlines, and flag overdue items, missing information, and workflow bottlenecks
  • Document repeatable processes and help maintain SOPs
  • Support data entry, quality checks, and record maintenance
  • Use AI tools to work faster, within the practice's privacy rules

What This Role Does Not Own

Determining licensing requirements, developing credentialing strategy, making hiring decisions, or managing payer contracts. You support those functions and the team owns the decisions.

Requirements

What You Bring

  • Prior experience supporting a US-based healthcare organization, particularly a telehealth company, medical practice, or patient services team
  • Experience working with both patients and clinicians
  • Experience with an EHR or patient management system, plus tools such as Google Workspace, Slack, and Notion
  • Experience handling sensitive patient information and following HIPAA requirements
  • Excellent written and spoken English
  • Strong judgment about when to resolve an issue independently and when to escalate
  • Comfort using AI to speed up your work
  • Comfort working in a fast-paced startup where processes are still being developed
  • Experience coordinating healthcare administrative workflows, not only handling inbound calls, tickets, or data entry; backgrounds limited to call centers or scripted support are not a fit for this role
  • Available to work full-time during US business hours

Nice to Have

  • Experience in pediatrics, behavioral health, or specialty care
  • Experience with credentialing, payer enrollment, or license tracking
  • Experience with recruiting coordination or interview scheduling
  • Experience in an early-stage startup or a newly launched practice

How to Apply

Please include:

  1. Your updated resume
  2. A short Loom video (1 to 2 minutes) introducing yourself, describing the US healthcare organizations and EHR systems you have supported, and walking through a time you decided whether to resolve an issue yourself or escalate it, and why

Only candidates who submit a Loom video will be moved to the next step of the hiring process.

If you are organized, discreet, and have the judgment to keep patients and clinicians moving without needing everything spelled out, this role gives you the ownership and the direct impact to do your best work.

Benefits

Application Process Overview

Our comprehensive selection process ensures we find the right fit for both you and our clients:

  1. Initial Application - Submit your application and complete our prequalifying questions
  2. Video Introduction - Record a video introduction to showcase your communication skills and work experience
  3. Role-Specific Assessment - Complete a homework assignment tailored to the position (if applicable)
  4. Recruitment Interview - Initial screening with our talent team
  5. Executive Interview - Meet with senior leadership to discuss role alignment
  6. Client Interview - Final interview with the client team you'd be supporting
  7. Background & Reference Check - Professional reference verification
  8. Job Offer - Successful candidates receive a formal offer to join the team

Each stage is designed to evaluate your fit for the role while giving you insights into our company culture and expectations. We'll keep you informed throughout the process and provide feedback at each step.

jobs.description:
About the Role

We are seeking an exceptional graduate to join Stalis as a generalist across our technical and operational functions. You will work closely with teams across the business, developing a deep understanding of how healthcare data moves through our systems and identifying opportunities to apply programming, modern tooling, and AI to improve how we work. Over time, as Stalis’s data intelligence capability matures, you will have the opportunity to contribute directly to machine learning and analytics work that shapes our next generation of products.

The Reality of the Work

This is a broad role, and not every task will be glamorous. Much of the early value comes from genuinely understanding how work is done at Stalis today - which means doing the work, not just observing it. Some of your time will be spent on detailed, careful data tasks that are essential to our clients. The opportunity is to use that understanding as the foundation for automation, improvement, and new capability. The best ideas will come from the ground up, and we expect you to find them.

What you’ll actually do

  • Work alongside our data migration and engineering teams on live client projects, contributing to the day-to-day delivery of healthcare data work.
  • Identify inefficiencies, repetitive tasks, and fragile processes - and build the scripts, tools, and small systems that fix them.
  • Write and maintain code, primarily in Python & SQL, to automate workflows, process data, and support internal operations.
  • Apply and experiment with AI tooling - LLMs, embeddings, classifiers - to problems across the business where they add real value, and be honest about where they don’t.
  • Communicate your work clearly, in writing and in person, to colleagues who are not data scientists - so that your improvements get adopted rather than sidelined.
  • Over time, contribute to Stalis’s emerging data science and machine learning capability, including schema mapping, clinical data analytics, and data products.

Requirements

Who we’re looking for

You will need most, if not all, of the following:

  • Academic background. A strong degree from a top university in a quantitative or technical discipline - physics, engineering, computer science, mathematics, or similar.
  • Genuine technical aptitude. Comfortable writing code, and keen to write more of it. We are not looking for a particular stack or prior industry experience, but you should already be writing code for fun, coursework, or projects, and be able to pick up new tools quickly.
  • AI-savvy. Fluent with modern AI tools as a day-to-day part of how you work and think. You know what LLMs are good at, what they’re bad at, and how to use them without being credulous about their output.
  • Self-directed. You find problems, scope them yourself, and take them to a useful end state without being spoon-fed tasks. You are comfortable operating under ambiguity and choosing what to work on when it isn’t obvious.
  • Discerning and pragmatic. You can tell the difference between a problem worth solving properly and one worth a fifty-line script today. You don’t gold-plate.
  • Strong communicator, in writing especially. You can write a short memo or a handover document that brings people along. In a small, distributed business, this matters more than people think.
  • Emotionally intelligent. Improvements to how people work can feel like criticism, even when they aren’t. You can read a room, win people over, and work collaboratively with colleagues who know things you don’t.
  • Domain-humble. You are curious about how Stalis works today before you try to change it. You understand that experienced colleagues know things that aren’t written down, and you treat that knowledge as an asset.

Benefits

What you’ll get from us

  • Unusual breadth of exposure for a graduate role - you will see how a specialist healthcare data company actually runs, from the data up.
  • A path into machine learning and data science work as Stalis’s data intelligence capability develops, with real problems and real data to work on.
  • Direct access to senior colleagues, reporting to the Head of Data Science, and genuine influence over how the company evolves.
  • A role that will grow as quickly as you do.

jobs.description:
Who We Are

Flosum is a bootstrapped, profitable B2B SaaS company building the leading Salesforce-native DevSecOps, Data Protection, and Security platform. Our solutions are trusted by Fortune 500 enterprises in the most heavily regulated industries on the planet — financial services, healthcare, government, and insurance.

We’re not a startup burning cash and chasing vanity metrics. We’re a proven, scaling business that reached profitability on our own terms. As a Salesforce Summit Partner and Innovation Award winner, we’ve earned our seat at the table alongside the biggest names in enterprise software.

Built 100% on the Salesforce platform. Serving enterprises that demand zero compromise on security, compliance, and reliability.

Why This Role Exists

We are entering an aggressive growth phase — expanding our product surface, deepening our platform capabilities, and accelerating our delivery velocity. We need senior-caliber Node.js developers who can own significant parts of our architecture and ship production code that enterprise customers depend on daily.

This is not a staff augmentation seat. You will work directly with engineering leadership, product managers, and the CEO. Your decisions will have real consequences, your opinions will be heard, and your craftsmanship will be visible to the customers who rely on our platform.

What You’ll Build

  • High-performance backend services and APIs powering enterprise-grade SaaS applications
  • Scalable, secure Node.js micro services and integrations within the Salesforce ecosystem
  • Modern front-end experiences using Vue.js and TypeScript that serve demanding enterprise users
  • CI/CD pipeline tooling, automation frameworks, and developer productivity infrastructure
  • Real-time data processing and event-driven architectures handling sensitive enterprise data at scale

Requirements

Read this section carefully. We are specific about what we need because we are serious about who we hire.

Non-Negotiable Technical Requirements

  • 5+ years of professional Node.js development in production environments — not tutorials, not side projects, not bootcamp exercises. Real production systems serving real users at scale.
  • Expert-level understanding of asynchronous programming, event loops, streams, and the Node.js runtime. You should be able to explain backpressure, the differences between setImmediate and process.nextTick, and why unhandled promise rejections are dangerous — without Googling it.
  • Deep experience with TypeScript in production codebases. We write typed code, and we expect you to understand why.
  • Strong command of RESTful API design, authentication patterns (OAuth 2.0, JWT), and API security best practices for enterprise environments.
  • Proven experience with SQL and NoSQL databases, query optimization, data modeling, and understanding the performance implications of schema decisions at scale.
  • Proficiency with Git workflows, code review practices, automated testing (unit, integration, and end-to-end), and CI/CD pipelines.
  • Solid understanding of containerization (Docker), cloud services (AWS/GCP/Azure), and infrastructure-as-code principles.

Highly Preferred (These Will Set You Apart)

  • Salesforce development experience: Apex, Lightning Web Components (LWC), Visualforce, or Salesforce API integrations. If you know both Node.js and Salesforce, you are a rare and extremely valuable candidate to us.
  • Experience building or contributing to Salesforce ISV (AppExchange) products.
  • Vue.js front-end development experience, particularly with Vue 3 Composition API and state management.
  • Experience working in B2B SaaS companies serving enterprise customers with strict compliance requirements (SOC 2, HIPAA, FedRAMP, GDPR).
  • Familiarity with DevOps/DevSecOps toolchains and practices in the Salesforce ecosystem.

The Kind of Person We’re Looking For

Skills get you in the door. Mindset determines whether you thrive here:

Missionary, Not Mercenary

You care about what you’re building and why. You take ownership not because someone assigned it to you, but because that’s who you are. When something is broken at 2 AM, you don’t check whether it’s “your responsibility” — you fix it.

Builder, Not a Bystander

You don’t wait for perfect specifications. You dig in, ask hard questions, propose solutions, and ship. You would rather have a working prototype by Friday than a polished slide deck by next quarter.

Craftsperson Under Pressure

Enterprise customers depend on our uptime and data integrity. You write code that doesn’t just work — it survives. You understand that in regulated industries, your code is your reputation.

Direct Communicator

You say what you think, respectfully and clearly. If a technical decision is wrong, you speak up — regardless of who made it. We value candor over politeness-at-the-expense-of-quality.

This Is a Long-Term Commitment

Let us be direct: we are not looking for contractors who jump between projects every few months. We are building a world-class engineering team, and we invest heavily in the people who join us. In return, we expect commitment.

This role is designed as a long-term, full-time engagement. You will grow with us. You will own systems end-to-end. You will see the direct impact of your work in how Fortune 500 companies build, protect, and deploy on Salesforce.

If you’re looking for a short-term gig while you wait for something else, this isn’t the role. If you want to build something that matters and be part of a team that’s scaling from strong to dominant, keep reading.

Benefits

What We Offer

  • Competitive compensation commensurate with your experience and impact
  • Direct collaboration with the founding team and engineering leadership — your voice will carry weight from day one
  • A profitable, stable company with aggressive growth plans — no funding anxiety, no runway clock
  • The opportunity to work on enterprise-grade products used by some of the largest organizations in the world
  • Meaningful technical challenges: security, compliance, scale, and reliability at the intersection of Node.js and Salesforce
  • A culture that rewards ownership, speed, and craftsmanship over politics and hierarchy
  • Remote-first flexibility with a results-oriented work environment

Elevate Teams is a fast-growing U.S. company that connects independent insurance agencies with highly skilled bilingual virtual assistants from Latin America. We help agencies scale their operations while creating meaningful remote career opportunities for talented professionals around the world.

Elevate Teams is building a new web product for independent insurance agencies. It has work queues, intake, a process library, dashboards, and AI agents that draft work for people to approve. You would be the first engineer on it and you would own a lane: a whole area of the product, from database to screen.

jobs.title: Senior Security GRC Engineer
jobs.description:
Why Mozilla?

Mozilla Corporation is the non-profit-backed technology company that has shaped the internet for the better over the last 25 years. We make pioneering brands like Firefox, the privacy-minded web browser. Now, with more than 225 million people around the world using our products each month, we're shaping the next 25 years of technology and helping to reclaim an internet built for people, not companies. Our work focuses on diverse areas including AI, social media, security and more. And we're doing this while never losing our focus on our core mission – to make the internet better for people.

The Mozilla Corporation is wholly owned by the non-profit 501(c) Mozilla Foundation. This means we aren't beholden to any shareholders — only to our mission. Along with thousands of volunteer contributors and collaborators all over the world, Mozillians design, build and distribute open-source software that enables people to enjoy the internet on their terms.

About this team and role:

The role is part of the Security Function within the broader Mozilla Infrastructure team. The Security team supports Product, Enterprise and GRC functions across the organization aligned with the mission to build a safe & secure internet. This role is responsible for defining, developing and helping implement a Governance, Risk and Compliance framework for both Enterprise and Product verticals. The ideal candidate will be responsible to deliver an integrated framework that aligns security, privacy, regulatory, and risk management initiatives across the organization. This is an ideal role for someone early in their GRC or security career who is curious, organized, and eager to take on a wide range of work. You’ll get broad exposure across risk, audit, and a growing set of security programs.

What you'll do:

Risk Management

  • Perform risk assessments and process incoming risk questions and intake requests
  • Maintain the risk register, keeping entries accurate, current, and well documented
  • Track risk treatment plans and follow up with owners on progress
  • Manage the exceptions and issues tracking process, including intake, documentation, expiration follow-up, and reporting
  • Support third-party risk activities, such as vendor assessments, questionnaire review, and tracking remediation

Compliance and Audit

  • Coordinate evidence collection from control owners and chase outstanding requests
  • Help prepare control owners and stakeholders for audit interviews
  • Keep the SOC 2 system description, ISMS documentation, and Statement of Applicability (SoA) up to date
  • Track audit gaps and findings and drive remediation to closure with control owners

Security Program Support

  • Help GRC and partner teams run governance for the Secure Software Development Lifecycle (SSDLC), including tracking adoption, gathering evidence, and maintaining supporting standards
  • Support data classification and data governance efforts by maintaining documentation, tracking adoption, and coordinating with data owners
  • Assist with business impact analysis (BIA) and business continuity/disaster recovery (BC/DR) activities, including plan maintenance, exercise coordination, and follow-up on gaps
  • Track vulnerability management metrics and remediation status, and follow up with system owners on overdue items
  • Help coordinate penetration testing engagements, from scoping and scheduling through findings tracking and remediation follow-up

GRC Operations and Tooling

  • Serve as an administrator for our GRC platform, including users, workflows, integrations, and reporting
  • Identify opportunities to streamline processes and automate repetitive GRC work
  • Help maintain policies, standards, and supporting documentation

What you'll bring:

  • Experience in cybersecurity, GRC, IT audit, or a related field (typically 2-4 years)
  • Working knowledge of security and compliance frameworks such as SOC 2, ISO 27001, or NIST
  • Familiarity with risk assessment concepts and the risk management lifecycle
  • Strong organization and follow-through, with the ability to juggle many workstreams and deadlines at once
  • Clear written and verbal communication, and comfort working with technical and non-technical stakeholders
  • A collaborative, curious mindset and a genuine desire to learn and take on new challenges
  • Hands-on experience with a GRC platform (e.g., Vanta, Drata, OneTrust, ServiceNow GRC, or similar)
  • Experience supporting an audit (SOC 2, ISO 27001, or similar)
  • Exposure to any of: vulnerability management, third-party risk, BC/DR, secure development practices, or penetration test coordination
  • Scripting or automation skills (e.g., Python, SQL, or workflow tools) to improve GRC processes
  • A relevant certification or one in progress (e.g., Security+, CISA, CISM, CISSP)
What you'll get:

  • Rich medical, dental, and vision coverage.
  • Generous retirement contributions with 100% immediate vesting (regardless of whether you contribute).

  • Build polished, responsive user experiences using React and Next.js.

  • Deep PostgreSQL/database engineering experience.

  • Experience working with financial or high-stakes transactional systems, such as fintech, payments, billing, payroll, or ledgering.

About the Role

At Pavago, one of our clients is hiring a Customer Success & Client Retention Specialist to strengthen client relationships, improve the customer experience, and reduce churn.

This role is focused on what happens after a client comes onboard — making sure customers see value, stay engaged, receive proactive support, and have compelling reasons to continue the relationship.

You’ll work closely with leadership, sales, and operations to improve the customer journey from onboarding through long-term retention.

If you have experience in Customer Success, Account Management, Client Retention, or Customer Experience and enjoy building lasting client relationships, this could be a strong fit.

Customer Success & Relationship Management

  • Identify potential issues before they become reasons for churn
  • Ensure clients consistently receive a responsive and professional experience

Client Retention & Churn Reduction

  • Develop and execute strategies to improve client retention
  • Identify customers who may be disengaged or at risk of leaving

Monitor and report on metrics such as:

  • Client retention rate
  • Customer churn
  • NPS
  • CSAT
  • Customer engagement
  • Renewal performance

Use customer data and feedback to identify trends, risks, and opportunities for improvement.

jobs.title: Senior Node.js Developer (Romania)
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Flosum is a bootstrapped, profitable B2B SaaS company building the leading Salesforce-native DevSecOps, Data Protection, and Security platform. Our solutions are trusted by Fortune 500 enterprises in the most heavily regulated industries on the planet — financial services, healthcare, government, and insurance.

We’re not a startup burning cash and chasing vanity metrics. We’re a proven, scaling business that reached profitability on our own terms. As a Salesforce Summit Partner and Innovation Award winner, we’ve earned our seat at the table alongside the biggest names in enterprise software.

Built 100% on the Salesforce platform. Serving enterprises that demand zero compromise on security, compliance, and reliability.

Why This Role Exists

We are entering an aggressive growth phase — expanding our product surface, deepening our platform capabilities, and accelerating our delivery velocity. We need senior-caliber Node.js developers who can own significant parts of our architecture and ship production code that enterprise customers depend on daily.

This is not a staff augmentation seat. You will work directly with engineering leadership, product managers, and the CEO. Your decisions will have real consequences, your opinions will be heard, and your craftsmanship will be visible to the customers who rely on our platform.

What You’ll Build

  • High-performance backend services and APIs powering enterprise-grade SaaS applications
  • Scalable, secure Node.js micro services and integrations within the Salesforce ecosystem
  • Modern front-end experiences using Vue.js and TypeScript that serve demanding enterprise users
  • CI/CD pipeline tooling, automation frameworks, and developer productivity infrastructure
  • Real-time data processing and event-driven architectures handling sensitive enterprise data at scale

Requirements

Read this section carefully. We are specific about what we need because we are serious about who we hire.

Non-Negotiable Technical Requirements

  • 5+ years of professional Node.js development in production environments — not tutorials, not side projects, not bootcamp exercises. Real production systems serving real users at scale.
  • Expert-level understanding of asynchronous programming, event loops, streams, and the Node.js runtime. You should be able to explain backpressure, the differences between setImmediate and process.nextTick, and why unhandled promise rejections are dangerous — without Googling it.
  • Deep experience with TypeScript in production codebases. We write typed code, and we expect you to understand why.
  • Strong command of RESTful API design, authentication patterns (OAuth 2.0, JWT), and API security best practices for enterprise environments.
  • Proven experience with SQL and NoSQL databases, query optimization, data modeling, and understanding the performance implications of schema decisions at scale.
  • Proficiency with Git workflows, code review practices, automated testing (unit, integration, and end-to-end), and CI/CD pipelines.
  • Solid understanding of containerization (Docker), cloud services (AWS/GCP/Azure), and infrastructure-as-code principles.

Highly Preferred (These Will Set You Apart)

  • Salesforce development experience: Apex, Lightning Web Components (LWC), Visualforce, or Salesforce API integrations. If you know both Node.js and Salesforce, you are a rare and extremely valuable candidate to us.
  • Experience building or contributing to Salesforce ISV (AppExchange) products.
  • Vue.js front-end development experience, particularly with Vue 3 Composition API and state management.
  • Experience working in B2B SaaS companies serving enterprise customers with strict compliance requirements (SOC 2, HIPAA, FedRAMP, GDPR).
  • Familiarity with DevOps/DevSecOps toolchains and practices in the Salesforce ecosystem.

The Kind of Person We’re Looking For

Skills get you in the door. Mindset determines whether you thrive here:

Missionary, Not Mercenary

You care about what you’re building and why. You take ownership not because someone assigned it to you, but because that’s who you are. When something is broken at 2 AM, you don’t check whether it’s “your responsibility” — you fix it.

Builder, Not a Bystander

You don’t wait for perfect specifications. You dig in, ask hard questions, propose solutions, and ship. You would rather have a working prototype by Friday than a polished slide deck by next quarter.

Craftsperson Under Pressure

Enterprise customers depend on our uptime and data integrity. You write code that doesn’t just work — it survives. You understand that in regulated industries, your code is your reputation.

Direct Communicator

You say what you think, respectfully and clearly. If a technical decision is wrong, you speak up — regardless of who made it. We value candor over politeness-at-the-expense-of-quality.

This Is a Long-Term Commitment

Let us be direct: we are not looking for contractors who jump between projects every few months. We are building a world-class engineering team, and we invest heavily in the people who join us. In return, we expect commitment.

This role is designed as a long-term, full-time engagement. You will grow with us. You will own systems end-to-end. You will see the direct impact of your work in how Fortune 500 companies build, protect, and deploy on Salesforce.

If you’re looking for a short-term gig while you wait for something else, this isn’t the role. If you want to build something that matters and be part of a team that’s scaling from strong to dominant, keep reading.

Benefits

What We Offer

  • Competitive compensation commensurate with your experience and impact
  • Direct collaboration with the founding team and engineering leadership — your voice will carry weight from day one
  • A profitable, stable company with aggressive growth plans — no funding anxiety, no runway clock
  • The opportunity to work on enterprise-grade products used by some of the largest organizations in the world
  • Meaningful technical challenges: security, compliance, scale, and reliability at the intersection of Node.js and Salesforce
  • A culture that rewards ownership, speed, and craftsmanship over politics and hierarchy
  • Remote-first flexibility with a results-oriented work environment

Remote: Experity offers Team Members the opportunity to work remotely or in an office.


The role comes at an inflection point. Experity is moving from a legacy processor model to a Payment Facilitator (PayFac) model with Fiserv, which includes rolling out new devices and launching new payment capabilities. The Director will lead that transition while keeping current clients stable - then build the team, processes, and controls the program needs to operate at scale. The Director will partner across multiple departments – including Product – Product owns how payments work in the Experity product line, while this role owns how the payments business runs.


Responsibilities:


Payments strategy and program ownership


  • Own the Experity Payments program end to end, including its revenue, margin, and client outcomes.
  • Set the operational roadmap and priorities, balancing near-term execution with long-term capability growth.
  • Act as the decision point for payments issues, tradeoffs, and dependencies across the business.
  • Partner with the Payments Product Manager and coordiante with internal teams on client related needs and opportunities.

PayFac transition and new capabilities


  • Lead the move to the PayFac model, including onboarding, underwriting, compliance, device, and system readiness.
  • Drive the PayFac device migration program, and launch new Surcharge capabilities and pricing model.
  • Manage the transition from the legacy gateway resulting in no business disruption for current clientele.

Operations, onboarding, and client support

  • Lead the teams that onboard merchants, monitor risk, and resolve payment issues.
  • Own the escalation path for complex client issues, driving root cause and resolution.
  • Build documented, repeatable processes and operating procedures
  • Identify where automation or AI can reduce manual work.

Vendor and partner management


  • Own relationships with the processor, sponsor bank, gateway, compliance, and hardware partners.
  • Hold vendors to service levels and contract terms, and align their roadmaps with Experity's needs.
  • Drive revenue growth through business development with current and prospective partners, including partners processing on Experity payment rails, and support enterprise sales.

Compliance and risk

  • Serve as the accountable owner for payments compliance, including merchant agreements, AML, complaint handling, third-party oversight, and card network and sponsor bank requirements.
  • Keep audit, attestation, and underwriting materials current and ready for review.

Hardware and device operations


  • Own the payment device lifecycle: strategy, procurement, ordering, fulfillment, tracking, and fleet management.
  • Plan inventory against onboarding pace so devices are never the constraint on growth.

Commercial governance, reporting, and enablement

  • Set pricing and fee guardrails with Finance and Sales, and approve exceptions within delegated authority.
  • Maintain dashboards on revenue, margin, volume, active merchants, and adoption, and report to senior leadership.
  • Equip Sales, Implementation, Support, and Client Success with training and documentation on merchant agreements, fees and terms, and payment device support.

Deliverables:

  • First 90 Days:
    • Takes ownership of active PayFac, surcharge, and device workstreams with no loss of momentum.
    • Establishes working relationships and escalation paths with each key vendor and internal partner.
    • Delivers a clear view of program health (revenue, margin, volume, risks) to senior leadership.
    • Documents decision rights and core processes that currently live with one person.
  • First Year:
    • PayFac model live and scaling with surcharging adopted by target clients.
    • Legacy gateway transition managed without client disruption.
    • Payments revenue and margin growing against plan.
    • Team structured with clear roles and backup coverage for every critical function.
    • Compliance and partner obligation met with clean audit and attestation results.

Education:

  • Bachelor's degree in business or finance or equivalent combination of education and experience.

Experience:


  • 10+ years in payments, merchant services, or fintech operations, with 5+ years leading teams.
  • Direct experience operating within, or launching, a Payment Facilitator (PayFac) or ISO program.
  • Working knowledge of card network rules, interchange and pricing models, merchant underwriting, PCI DSS, and AML/KYC requirements.
  • Experience managing processors, sponsor banks, and gateway partners, including contract terms and escalations.
  • Experience running a payments P&L or owning revenue and margin metrics.
  • Proven ability to lead cross-functional initiatives across Product, Finance, Sales, and Support.
  • Comfortable being hands-on: resolving escalations, reviewing agreements, and building processes from scratch.
  • Clear communicator who can explain payments economics to executives and clients alike.

​Preferred:

  • Embedded or vertical SaaS payments experience, ideally in healthcare or patient payments.
  • Experience with Fiserv, a sponsor bank such as Pathward, or comparable processor and bank partners.
  • Hands-on surcharging, card-present, and e-commerce payment launches.
  • Payment device and terminal fleet management experience.
  • Familiarity with Salesforce and billing or agreement systems.
  • Payments certifications such as CPP (Certified Payments Professional) or compliance credentials such as CAMS.

Travel:

jobs.title: Senior Model Risk Analyst, AI & Model Risk
jobs.description:
Block is one company built from many blocks, all united by the same purpose: economic empowerment. We build technology that increases access and independence for sellers, individuals, and artists around the world. Working at Block means working on and across our brands—Square, Cash App, Afterpay, TIDAL, Spiral, and Proto— in roles that connect, enable, and push all of them forward faster.

We’re remote-first by design and operate with intelligence at the center of everything we do. At Block, you'll be challenged by some of the brightest, most creative minds in the industry and have the tools and autonomy to do the most meaningful work of your career.

The Role

This role puts you at the center of the team that independently challenges the models Square Financial Services relies on, from the credit models that decide who gets a loan to the forecasting models that shape the bank's plans. You'll help work out how to validate modeling approaches that are new to banking, often before an industry playbook exists. And with broad access to AI tools that few banks offer, you'll help rethink how validation itself gets done, so our team can run a rigorous program efficiently. If you enjoy digging into data and code, forming your own view of how a model really behaves, and explaining that view clearly to developers, leaders and bank examiners, this is the place to be.

As a Senior Model Risk Analyst, you will lead independent validations of models used across Square Financial Services (SFS), Block's bank, which lends to small businesses through Square Loans and to consumers through Cash App Borrow, and offers FDIC-insured deposits. Every SFS model must be independently reviewed and approved before it goes into use, so your work directly affects whether the bank can launch new products, grow lending and meet regulatory expectations safely and on time. You will report to the Head of AI & Model Risk and join the AI & Model Risk team, part of the bank's independent risk function. No two validations are alike: you will decide which tests matter for each model's data, methodology and intended use, with minimal day-to-day oversight.

You Will

  • Lead independent validations across the model lifecycle, scaling the depth of your work to each model's risk rating
  • Validate models used across the bank, including credit underwriting and loss forecasting models for small business and consumer lending, and finance models used for business planning, stress testing and balance sheet management
  • Evaluate conceptual soundness: methodology, data, assumptions, limitations and any management adjustments to model outputs
  • Verify that models work as intended: reproduce developer code (typically Python), test input data for accuracy and completeness with SQL, confirm outputs, and review evidence of accurate implementation, data integrity controls and security
  • Build independent benchmark or challenger models for high-risk models, and perform outcomes analysis such as backtesting and rank-ordering tests
  • Independently review each model owner's proposed risk rating and recommend a final rating
  • Assess ongoing monitoring plans and results, review vendor models and pre-approved model changes, and flag models that are deteriorating before they become a problem
  • Write clear validation reports, rate findings by severity, agree on remediation with model owners and track it to closure
  • Present your conclusions to model owners, senior management and the bank's risk committees, and support internal audits and FDIC examinations
  • Help keep the model inventory and validation records accurate, and build AI-enabled tools that make the validation program faster and more scalable

You Have

  • A minimum of 5 years of related experience with a Bachelor's degree in a quantitative field such as mathematics, statistics, data science, economics, finance or computer science; or 3 years and a Master's degree; or a PhD without experience; or equivalent work experience in model development, model validation or quantitative analysis
  • Hands-on experience developing or validating statistical and machine learning models, and in-depth knowledge of the quantitative methods used to test them
  • Proficiency in Python and SQL, including working in and adapting code someone else wrote, plus familiarity with GitHub
  • Experience with one or more of these model types: credit underwriting, loss forecasting, stress testing, asset liability management or interest rate risk, or financial planning and forecasting
  • Strong technical writing, and the ability to explain complex model issues to non-technical partners, senior management and regulators
  • Sound judgment to scope a validation, choose the right tests and manage several validations at once

Nice to Have

  • Model development or validation experience at a bank or fintech
  • Knowledge of interagency model risk management guidance, including SR 26-2
  • Experience building challenger models, especially machine learning models
  • Experience validating vendor models
  • Prior second-line-of-defense or internal audit experience at a bank or financial institution
  • Certifications such as FRM or PRM

Technologies We Use and Teach

Block is investing heavily in AI, and our workflows are evolving accordingly. You'll have broad access to AI tools, use them in your own validation work, help design how the team uses them, and see up close how the bank governs AI alongside traditional models.

Block takes a market-based approach to pay, and pay may vary depending on your location. U.S. locations are categorized into one of four zones based on a cost of labor index for that geographic area. Application Guidelines

Candidates may submit up to 9 active applications within a 60-day period. Reapplications to the same role are accepted 90 days after a previous application has been reviewed.

Use of AI in Our Hiring Process

We may use automated AI tools to evaluate job applications for efficiency and consistency. These tools comply with local regulations, including bias audits, and we handle all personal data in accordance with state and local privacy laws.

Contact us here with hiring practice or data usage questions.

Every benefit we offer is designed with one goal: empowering you to do the best work of your career while building the life you want. Remote work, medical insurance, flexible time off, retirement savings plans, and modern family planning are just some of our offering. Check out our other benefits at Block.

Square makes commerce and financial services accessible to sellers. Cash App is the easy way to spend, send, and store money. Afterpay is transforming the way customers manage their spending over time. TIDAL is a music platform that empowers artists to thrive as entrepreneurs. jobs.title: AI Enablement Engineer
jobs.description:
Overview

Impact the Moment

We're looking for an AI Enablement Engineer to join our AI Enablement team; someone who embeds directly with business teams to understand how they work today, and helps them reimagine those workflows using AI. This is fundamentally an engineering role, but the job isn't to build a custom solution for every workflow you touch. It is to turn what you learn into repeatable patterns, reusable proof of concepts, and skills that let teams keep moving on their own.

In the near term, you'll help support the rollout of our enterprise AI tools across the organization, working through the technical details of onboarding and adoption. But the real mandate is longer term and bigger: helping the company become genuinely AI native by continuously finding where AI tools, existing ones and new ones as they arrive, can meaningfully change how business teams get work done, and then building the patterns that make those changes scale.

This role sits between engineering and the business. You need enough technical depth to build real prototypes and understand how these tools work under the hood, and enough business fluency to sit with a team, understand their workflow, and help them see a genuinely different way of working. We're also looking for someone who is an expert-level practitioner of our enterprise AI tools, especially M365 Copilot and Claude, not just someone who knows about them. You should be able to get more out of these tools than most people at the company, and use that depth to show others what's actually possible.

This is a remote position open to applicants authorized to work for any employer within the United States.

What You'll Do:

Enterprise Tool Rollout (Near Term)

  • Support the technical rollout of our enterprise AI tools: onboarding, integrations, access issues, and the practical problems that come up as teams start using it.
  • Build early proof of concepts with pilot teams that show what the tool can do for their specific workflows.
  • Partner with other functions like cybersecurity, legal, data ethics and training on the rollout so the technical details don't become adoption blockers.

Workflow Reimagination & Forward Deployment (Ongoing)

  • Embed with business teams to understand their workflows in depth, and identify where AI can change how the work gets done, not just speed up one step in an old process.
  • Design and build proof of concepts that show a team a genuinely new way of working, then help them carry it into everyday use.
  • Identify and enable foundational capabilities like connectors and any other integrations.
  • Turn what works into repeatable patterns: reusable prompt libraries, skills, plugins, workflow templates, integration recipes, and reference builds that other teams can pick up without needing a dedicated engineer.
  • Feed what you learn from the field back into company-wide best practices, training, and governance, in partnership with the rest of the AI Enablement team.
  • Teach and transfer knowledge, not just solutions: help teams build enough AI fluency to extend and adapt what you've built themselves.
  • Scout new AI tools and capabilities as they become available within the company, and form a clear point of view on what's worth enabling and where.
  • Guide teams toward optimal, cost-efficient use of enterprise AI tools: right-sized models, well-scoped prompts, and workflows that get strong results without wasting spend.

Who You Are

  • An expert-level practitioner of enterprise AI tools like M365 Copilot and Claude: you know these tools inside and out, push them well past basic use cases, and can teach others how to do the same.
  • A real engineering background: you can prototype, script, and build integrations yourself, not just advise on what's technically possible.
  • A product mindset: you default to designing and building for reuse and self-service rather than one-off solutions for a single team.
  • Comfortable embedding with a business team long enough to deeply understand their workflow, but disciplined about generalizing what you build so it outlives that one engagement.
  • Strong proof-of-concept instincts: you'd rather get something real in front of users quickly than over-engineer before you know it's worth building.
  • Curious and fast-moving with new AI tools and capabilities, comfortable evaluating and adopting new ones as the landscape shifts.
  • A strong communicator who can sit with a non-technical business team and guide them through rethinking how they work.

What You'll Learn & How You'll Grow

  • Deep, hands-on exposure to how a wide range of business workflows actually work across the company, and practice redesigning them around AI.
  • Practical expertise in building reusable AI patterns, accelerators, and evaluation approaches that scale beyond a single engagement.
  • Experience as a forward deployed engineer, a skill set that combines technical depth with business fluency and is in high demand.
  • The chance to help shape the technical patterns and playbook that the entire AI Enablement function relies on as it grows.

What Success Looks Like

  • Business teams have genuinely reimagined workflows using AI, not just automated a step of their old process.
  • A growing library of reusable AI enablement patterns and proof of concepts is adopted across the company, reducing the need for one-off engineering support.
  • The enterprise AI tool rollout lands smoothly, and the technical foundation is in place for the broader, longer-term AI enablement mandate.

Why work for us?

The work you do at McGraw Hill will be work that matters. We are collectively building experiences that will help shape the future of education. Play your part and experience a sense of fulfilment that will inspire you to even greater heights.

The pay range for this position is between $110,000 - $140,000 annually, however, base pay offered may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and location. jobs.title: Program Manager
jobs.description:
Correlation One develops workforce skills for the AI economy

Enterprises and governments work with us to develop talent and close critical data, digital, and technology skills gaps. Our global programs, including training programs and data competitions, also empower underrepresented communities and accelerate careers.

Our mission is to create equal access to the data-driven jobs of the future. We partner with top employers and government organizations to make that a reality, including Amazon, Coca-Cola, Johnson & Johnson, the U.S. State Department, and the U.S. Department of Defense.

Our skills training programs are 100% free for learners and are delivered virtually by industry experts to minimize traditional barriers to career advancement. We take pride in fostering supportive, human-led, group learning environments that build technical proficiency and confidence in participants.

Join us and let's shape the AI Economy together!

Your Impact:

As Program Manager (PM) at Correlation One, you will contribute to the success of our live, online training programs by managing key aspects of program delivery and supporting the Program Operations team in strategic initiatives. You will play a crucial role in the preparation, launch, and ongoing management of training programs, ensuring effective collaboration across teams and exceptional customer service.

The ideal candidate is an excellent project and program manager and is able to execute simultaneous competing deadlines and tasks involving multiple stakeholders. This role will support the preparation and launch of Correlation One training programs, including application setup and management, instructional staff hiring, cross-functional team collaboration, and client communication.

Reporting to a Senior Program Manager, this position requires a motivated individual with program management experience. A successful PM is a quick learner with a strong work ethic who takes initiative and is able to navigate ambiguity productively and patiently. They have an interest in changing lives through education and a desire to work on larger and/or different programs as we continue to scale. Correlation One is a company where creativity, initiative, collaboration, and communication are valued.

Key Responsibilities:

-Program Management

  • Assist in the preparation and launch of training programs, handling application setup, client communications, and managing instructional staff hiring processes.
  • Oversee multiple programs simultaneously, managing project timelines and ensuring seamless execution.
  • Support the Senior Operations Team in developing and implementing strategic initiatives to enhance program impact, experience, and scalability.
  • Facilitate a successful admissions process, which includes application setup and launch, applicant pipeline monitoring and reporting, and marketing initiatives, Q&A sessions, and/or any necessary applicant support to ensure strong enrollment.
  • Manage the instructional contractor screening, review, and hiring processes for Teaching Assistants and Lead Instructors.
  • Manage the live, online training programs (typically 12-20 weeks in length), ensuring learners, teaching assistants, instructors, and other stakeholders engage and benefit from the program.
  • Monitor learners’ progress in the course while providing support for instructors and other contractual staff.
  • Ensure stakeholders are fulfilling their role’s responsibilities and course technology is functioning appropriately.
  • Create a friendly, professional learning environment by troubleshooting learner needs and responding to all inquiries in a timely, professional manner.

-Admissions Process:

  • Contribute to a successful admissions process, including application setup, monitoring applicant pipelines, responding to Zendesk inquiries, and participating in marketing initiatives.
  • Work collaboratively with the Senior Program Manager on Q&A sessions and applicant support to ensure strong enrollment.

-Team Leadership and Development:

  • Manage and provide guidance to a small team of 1-2 Operations Analysts.
  • Foster a collaborative and innovative team culture, encouraging continuous learning and development.
  • Provide ongoing feedback, career development, and mentorship to team members.

-Client Relationship Management:

  • Support the Senior Program Manager in cultivating and strengthening relationships with clients, ensuring their unique needs are met.
  • Collaborate with the Senior Program Manager to address client concerns and identify opportunities for program enhancements.

-Cross-functional Collaboration:

  • Collaborate with various teams, including Business Operations, Curriculum, Professional Development, Account Management, and others, to ensure coordinated program execution.
  • Provide input to drive improvements in the overall training program ecosystem.

-Strategic Insight and Reporting:

  • Contribute to the analysis of program performance metrics and provide insights to senior leadership.
  • Assist in reporting on program developments, successes, and challenges, contributing to data-driven decision-making processes.

-Continuous Improvement:

  • Identify opportunities for process optimization and innovation, driving continuous improvement in program delivery and experience.
  • Implement best practices and lessons learned from previous programs to enhance overall effectiveness.

Your Expertise:

  • Bachelor's degree preferred; Master’s degree in a relevant field is a plus.
  • 3-5 years of experience in program management, with at least 1 directly in an educational or training institution.
  • Experience leading and managing teams, demonstrating autonomy and success.
  • Proficient in Google Suite, MS Office Suite, Slack, and Zoom.
  • Experience with Data analysis, CRM or Salesforce, and other education-related software is a plus.

Time Commitment:

  • While we provide a lot of flexibility as a remote-first organization, and given the general needs of the training operations team, the guide for working hours align to the East Coast (Monday - Friday, 9AM - 6PM ET)
  • Given the nature of adult learners, occasional work on Saturdays is required. Compensatory time off is provided for this work.

Location:

  • Due to upcoming program geography, our strong preference for this Program Manager's location is Canada.

How we support our people

  • Insurance or subsidies based on country
  • Unlimited Time Off, with a minimum time off recommendation
  • Company-paid holidays
  • Official company-wide holiday for the last week of the calendar year
  • Access to free data skills training through our programs
  • A company culture that empowers individuals and embraces diversity through its core mission

The compensation range for this position is specific to location and takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions. These factors include (but are not limited to) location, experience, education and skill sets. A reasonable estimate of the annual salary for this role is $92,000 - $107,000 CAD.

jobs.title: Principal Blockchain, Payments & Exchange Architect Rust
jobs.description:
We are seeking a hands-on Senior Payments Infrastructure Engineer to take ownership of an existing payments backend and complete its integration, testing, and production deployment.

The role involves working with Rust-based microservices, financial ledgers, digital wallets, cryptocurrency transactions, Fireblocks custody infrastructure, and fiat payment integrations.

Responsibilities include completing payment processing and settlement functionality, implementing transaction reconciliation, managing wallet integrations, ensuring accurate balance accounting, and building reliable transaction recovery and monitoring systems.

The engineer will integrate existing financial services using REST and gRPC, troubleshoot distributed systems, complete end-to-end testing, and ensure the infrastructure is secure, scalable, and production-ready.

Strong experience with backend engineering, financial transaction systems, distributed architecture, and cryptocurrency payments is essential. Experience with Rust, Fireblocks, TigerBeetle, Solana, AWS, and institutional wallet infrastructure is highly desirable.

The ideal candidate can independently understand an existing codebase, resolve integration challenges, and deliver production-ready financial infrastructure without unnecessarily rebuilding completed systems.

  • 8+ years of professional backend engineering experience, including significant hands-on responsibility for production financial systems, payment infrastructure, cryptocurrency platforms, or digital asset services.
  • Proven experience building and operating financial transaction systems involving payment processing, settlement, reconciliation, and balance management.
  • Strong understanding of double-entry accounting and financial ledger architecture, including transaction consistency, idempotency, auditability, and failure recovery.
  • Production experience with digital wallets and cryptocurrency payments, including deposits, withdrawals, transfers, transaction signing, and secure key management.
  • Experience integrating Fireblocks or comparable institutional custody platforms, including custody APIs, wallet administration, transaction authorization, and security policies.
  • Advanced proficiency in Rust, Go, or another high-performance backend language, with demonstrated ability to work in Rust-based microservices.
  • Expertise in distributed systems, including REST, gRPC, asynchronous processing, concurrency, fault tolerance, and event-driven architectures.
  • Strong database engineering experience, including PostgreSQL or comparable transactional databases, ACID guarantees, concurrency control, and data integrity.
  • Production experience with AWS, Docker, CI/CD, monitoring, and infrastructure security, including deploying and troubleshooting mission-critical services.
  • Deep understanding of blockchain transaction infrastructure, cryptographic signing, wallet architecture, and secure digital asset transfers.
  • Experience integrating third-party financial services, including payment gateways, banking APIs, fiat on/off ramps, or cryptocurrency exchanges.
  • Strong security engineering knowledge, including encryption, access controls, secrets management, transaction authorization, and financial-system security practices.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently own complex production systems, investigate unfamiliar codebases, resolve integration problems, and deliver reliable infrastructure without unnecessary redesign.
  • Experience with automated integration and end-to-end testing for financial transactions, including duplicate processing, partial failures, reconciliation discrepancies, and recovery scenarios.
  • Strong technical documentation and communication skills, with demonstrated experience collaborating across backend, infrastructure, blockchain, and financial engineering teams.

Highly Preferred

  • Direct production experience with Fireblocks and TigerBeetle.
  • Hands-on Rust development in financial or high-throughput distributed systems.
  • Experience with Solana, SPL tokens, and blockchain wallet integrations.
  • Experience building cryptocurrency exchanges, payment orchestration platforms, custody infrastructure, or treasury systems.
  • Familiarity with KYC/AML, PCI DSS, and financial services compliance requirements.
  • Evidence of personally engineering and deploying financial infrastructure handling real customer funds at production scale.

Solutions not problems .

  • Creative problem solver who can courageously propose and support new ideas to our organization. Not interested in best practices, lets build something better!
  • Ability to adapt. An ideal candidate will welcome the opportunity to solve a broad range of problems using a wide array of technologies.
  • Comfortable with ambiguity, shifting priorities and general growing pains of an early-stage technology company
  • An exceptional entrepreneurial judgment that fosters independence over micro-management
  • Understanding of football and international sports a huge plus

Deferred compensation

This opportunity is designed for entrepreneurial, startup-minded engineers who want to help build a significant global business. This is not free work. Compensation is agreed upon and deferred until funding is secured, at which point it transitions to a competitive, normalized salary plus equity and OleX token ownership. Our entire team, including the founder, operates under this arrangement. This position is intended for individuals who understand the risks of an early-stage startup, are comfortable with uncertain funding timelines, and are motivated by the opportunity to build something substantial while participating in its long-term ownership and success.

Ole Ole is located in beautiful Austin Texas, however, this role requires some travel we are privately held and rapidly growing!

Company Description

OleOle is building a global social network and messaging platform for football fans. Our mission is to create a single global community where supporters can follow their club and country, connect with other fans, message and call each other, follow live matches, discover content, and ultimately access a broader ecosystem of football products and services.

The OleOle platform combines social networking, encrypted messaging, live scores, video, multilingual content, payments, digital wallets, AI, and Mini Programs designed around the global football community.

OleOle — Where Fans Kick Off.

jobs.title: Bilingual Solar Project Manager
jobs.description:
About SpartanX LLC

At SpartanX, our approach is straightforward: we pair top-of-the-line solar technology with unmatched value. We deliver reliable solutions for homeowners while empowering our teams to grow, lead, and make a lasting impact. To be a Spartan means to lead with purpose, embrace challenges, and create meaningful change. Our mission is driven by innovation, integrity, and a commitment to excellence in solar energy. Join our community of professionals shaping the future of clean energy, where every project reflects our promise of Solar Done Right.

Bilingual Solar Project Manager

Full-Time | Remote – U.S. Based |

About This Role

Great Project Managers don't wait for problems to find them. They anticipate challenges, take ownership, and drive results.

SpartanX is seeking an experienced, customer-focused Bilingual Solar Project Manager to oversee residential solar projects from contract execution through Permission to Operate (PTO).

As the primary point of contact for homeowners, you will be responsible for managing project progression, setting realistic expectations, resolving operational challenges, and delivering an exceptional customer experience throughout the entire solar journey.

We're looking for someone who understands residential solar operations, communicates with confidence, and possesses the ability to navigate difficult conversations while maintaining strong customer relationships.

The ideal candidate is proactive, resourceful, highly organized, and committed to seeing every project through to completion.

What You'll Do

Project Management & Execution

  • Take ownership of an assigned portfolio of residential solar projects from contract execution through PTO.
  • Manage project timelines, milestones, outstanding requirements, and dependencies.
  • Proactively identify potential delays and coordinate solutions before they impact project progression.
  • Monitor aging and stalled projects, establishing clear action plans to move them forward.
  • Review project documentation for accuracy, completeness, and operational readiness.
  • Maintain accountability for project follow-through and successful completion.
  • Manage competing priorities across a high-volume project pipeline.

Customer Experience & Communication

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for homeowners throughout the project lifecycle.
  • Provide proactive, accurate, and timely project updates in both English and Spanish.
  • Establish realistic expectations regarding project milestones, timelines, and potential delays.
  • Explain technical and operational processes in a clear, customer-friendly manner.
  • Build customer confidence through consistent communication, transparency, and follow-through.
  • Manage difficult conversations with professionalism, empathy, and confidence.
  • Take ownership of customer concerns and work toward timely, effective resolutions.
  • Maintain positive customer relationships, even when projects encounter unexpected challenges.

Escalation & De-Escalation Management

  • Recognize potential customer escalations and intervene proactively.
  • Utilize effective de-escalation techniques when communicating with frustrated or dissatisfied homeowners.
  • Investigate customer complaints to identify underlying issues rather than simply addressing immediate concerns.
  • Develop and communicate actionable resolution plans.
  • Coordinate with appropriate departments to resolve complex operational or customer-related issues.
  • Exercise sound judgment when determining when leadership involvement is necessary.
  • Maintain ownership of escalated concerns through resolution, ensuring customers receive appropriate follow-up.
  • Identify recurring customer concerns and recommend improvements to prevent future escalations.

Cross-Functional Coordination

  • Collaborate with Sales, Site Survey, Design, Engineering, Permitting, Scheduling, Installation, Electrical, Inspections, Service, and Interconnection teams.
  • Coordinate outstanding project requirements, corrections, approvals, and documentation.
  • Communicate with utility providers, Authorities Having Jurisdiction (AHJs), and third-party partners as needed.
  • Maintain visibility into departmental dependencies and their impact on project timelines.
  • Follow up on outstanding action items and communicate operational barriers to appropriate stakeholders.
  • Facilitate effective communication across departments to ensure projects continue progressing.

Reporting & Operational Accountability

  • Maintain accurate, up-to-date project records within company systems.
  • Document customer communications, commitments, escalations, and resolutions.
  • Monitor project performance, milestone completion, and outstanding deliverables.
  • Provide leadership with accurate updates regarding project status, risks, and operational challenges.
  • Identify recurring project delays and recommend process improvements.
  • Support departmental performance objectives related to project completion, customer satisfaction, and operational efficiency.

What We're Looking For

  • Previous residential solar industry experience required.
  • Fluency in both English and Spanish required.
  • Previous project management, project coordination, or operational management experience required.
  • Strong understanding of the residential solar project lifecycle, including permitting, installation, inspections, interconnection, and PTO.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage customer escalations and effectively de-escalate difficult situations.
  • Strong customer service, relationship management, and conflict resolution skills.
  • Excellent organizational and time-management abilities.
  • Ability to independently manage a high volume of active projects and competing priorities.
  • Strong analytical, critical-thinking, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to make sound decisions and exercise good judgment in challenging situations.
  • Exceptional attention to detail and consistent follow-through.
  • Experience with CRM platforms, project management software, and Microsoft Office.
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with multiple departments.
  • Strong sense of urgency, personal accountability, and ownership.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Direct residential solar project management experience.
  • Experience managing residential solar projects across multiple states and markets.
  • Familiarity with AHJ requirements, utility approvals, and interconnection processes.
  • Experience resolving complex operational and customer escalations.
  • Experience identifying process inefficiencies and implementing workflow improvements.
  • PMP certification is a plus but not required.

Schedule & Work Arrangement

  • Full-time, fully remote position.
  • Must be based in the United States.
  • Monday–Friday, occasional Saturdays when needed
  • Availability to support assigned markets and operational business hours.

What SpartanX Provides

  • Compensation based on experience and qualifications.
  • Fully remote work environment.
  • Ongoing training and professional development.
  • Opportunities for career growth and advancement.
  • Collaborative, team-focused culture built on accountability, professionalism, and operational excellence.
  • Opportunity to directly impact project success, customer satisfaction, and company growth.

Why SpartanX?

At SpartanX, we understand that homeowners aren't just purchasing a solar system—they're placing their trust in the people responsible for delivering it.

Our Project Managers are the connection between that promise and its execution. They bring departments together, remove obstacles, manage expectations, and ensure homeowners feel informed and supported throughout their solar journey.

We value professionals who take ownership, communicate with purpose, solve problems, and understand that accountability means seeing things through—not simply passing them along.

If you're an experienced residential solar professional who thrives on solving problems, building relationships, and getting projects across the finish line, we want to hear from you.

Solar Done Right.

Product Strategy & Platform Architecture

jobs.title: Senior Vice President of Partnerships
jobs.description:
Who We Are

The Constructive Dialogue Institute (CDI) is a nonpartisan nonprofit organization dedicated to equipping the next generation of Americans with the skills to communicate and collaborate across lines of difference. We work with U.S. colleges and universities by providing co-curricular programming for students, professional development for faculty and staff, and strategic guidance to leadership. Our goal is to foster constructive dialogue at every level of the institution and to create the conditions for lasting organizational change. CDI's research-backed programs, including evidence from three randomized controlled trials, have reached more than 270,000 learners at more than 200 colleges and universities. CDI was co-founded by Caroline Mehl and psychologist Jonathan Haidt, the bestselling author of The Righteous Mind and The Anxious Generation.

The Role

CDI is seeking a Senior Vice President of Partnerships to lead our sales team and bring CDI's work to more colleges and universities. Reporting to the Chief Growth Officer, you will own a multi-million-dollar annual revenue goal for new partnerships and expansions, lead and grow a team of four, support our largest deals, and design pricing, packaging, and the sales motion. This is a hands-on leadership role: you will work deals alongside your team and roll up your sleeves to level-up the function. It suits a Director, Senior Director, or Vice President ready for a broader role.

The team sells three kinds of offerings: (1) leadership offerings, including multi-year strategic advisory engagements built on the CDI Institutional Change Model (our biggest growth area) and the Leadership Institute for presidents; (2) professional development workshops and trainings for faculty, staff, and students; and (3) Campus Packages, recurring commitments giving campuses access to Perspectives, CDI's online learning program. The team reaches institutions directly, through state systems and higher education associations, and through expansion with existing partners.

You will build on solid foundations, including a CRM, a forecasting rhythm, and quarterly business reviews, and shape the sales function for CDI's next stage of growth. Over the next five years, you will help grow CDI's annual revenue from partnerships from about $5 million to $10 million.

In your first year, success means meeting the revenue goal; sharpening our go-to-market strategy and sales motion, including a pricing and packaging recommendation by the end of the third quarter; forecasting within 10% of actual results from the second quarter on, backed by qualified pipeline of three times the target for each of the next two quarters; and developing the team, including filling at least two new roles by mid-year.

What You’ll Do

Revenue Strategy and Sales Motion

  • Own the annual revenue goal for new partnerships and expansions: set targets with the Chief Growth Officer, translate them into goals and territories for each seller, and build the pipeline to reach them.

  • Run forecast and pipeline reviews with Revenue Operations, giving leaders an early, reliable view of the year.

  • Lead pricing and packaging, with the Chief Growth Officer's approval.

  • Build a repeatable sales motion for prospecting, qualification, and deal management.

Team Leadership

  • Recruit, coach, and hold accountable a team of senior sellers and a Partnerships Development Representative through one-on-ones, deal reviews, and quarterly business reviews.

  • Sell alongside the team: join discovery calls, sharpen deal strategy, coach negotiations, and help close.

  • Grow the team as revenue grows.

Strategic Deals and Channels

  • Personally lead or support CDI's most complex deals, including multi-campus and multi-year advisory engagements with presidents, provosts, and system leaders.

  • Oversee state system partnerships, led by the Vice President of Strategic Partnerships, and build relationships with governing boards and higher education associations. Represent CDI at national conferences.

  • Own expansion across CDI's partner base, including our largest strategic accounts, working closely with the teams that deliver for partners.

Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Partner with the Chief Growth Officer on segment priorities and long-term revenue plans.

  • Plan target accounts, campaigns, and conferences with Marketing & Communications, give feedback on lead quality, and share what you hear from prospective partners to sharpen CDI's messaging and inform the product and offering roadmap.

  • Work with Revenue Operations to keep partnership data accurate and handoffs clean.

Requirements

Who You Are

The first three qualities matter most. If you meet most of this, we encourage you to apply.

  • A sales leader with a track record. You have directly managed a team of three or more sellers who each carried a revenue target, and you grew their results.

  • A consultative seller who closes complex deals. You have closed large multi-stakeholder deals with long buying cycles, and you see prospects as partners. You quickly master CDI's value proposition and can sell both multi-year engagements and recurring programs. Experience with multi-campus agreements or pricing is a plus.

  • A builder who runs on data. You handle ambiguity well, build processes without bureaucracy, and forecast from data so CDI can move fast in a competitive field.

  • A coach who raises the bar. You coach each person to their strengths, give direct feedback, and make clear who owns each decision.

  • Ideally, higher education experience. Selling to colleges, universities, or state systems is strongly preferred; education technology experience is valued.

  • Mission-aligned. You connect with CDI's nonpartisan mission and believe commercial discipline and institutional impact reinforce each other. Nonprofit experience is welcome but not required.

What We Offer

  • A Mission-Driven Culture — our work culture genuinely reflects our mission, characterized by intellectual humility, continuous improvement, and open-mindedness

  • Unlimited PTO — recharge on your own schedule with unlimited paid time off, in addition to 13 company holidays

  • Health, Vision & Dental — health, vision, and dental plans through, with CDI contributing toward your premiums each month

  • 401(k) Match — invest in your future with a 100% match on your contributions, up to 3% of your pay

  • Professional Development — a generous annual budget to invest in your growth: build new skills, deepen existing ones, and stay inspired in your work

  • Remote Work Support — up to $500 reimbursed for home office equipment and up to $50/month reimbursed for home internet or cell phone expense

The Details

  • Compensation: $250,000 on-target earnings (OTE): a $200,000 base salary and $50,000 in target incentive pay, tied to team revenue results, not a personal quota, and to strategic goals such as forecast accuracy and team development

  • Reports to: Chief Growth Officer

  • Direct reports: Four growing to six+. Current team: Vice President of Strategic Partnerships, Senior Director of Partnerships, Director of Partnerships, and a Partnerships Development Representative (similar to an SDR or BDR). At least two additional team members will be hired in 2027.

  • Location and schedule: Full-time and remote, based in the U.S., with substantial overlap with Eastern time business hours

  • Travel: One to two trips per quarter for conferences and partner visits, plus two team gatherings a year

  • Target start date: February 2027

Highlights

CDI seeks a SVP of Partnerships to lead our higher ed sales team, own the earned revenue that funds our mission, and close our largest institutional deals. Remote, US-based, $250K OTE.
